facts.fact: Kashef Mahboob Chowdhury's Friendship Centre in Gaibandha, Bangladesh, dates from 2011.
facts.quote: 2011: Friendship Centre, Gaibandha, Bangladesh

facts.fact: The Friendship Centre won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in the 2014–16 cycle.
facts.quote: Aga Khan Award for Architecture, for Friendship Center 2014-16 Cycle

facts.fact: The complex stands in Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, the administrative capital, on an island in the Diyawanna Oya.
facts.quote: Situated in Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, the administrative capital, it is built on an island, surrounded by the Diyawanna Oya.

facts.fact: President J. R. Jayewardene invited Geoffrey Bawa to design the new Parliament building in 1979, and it was completed in 1982 with Japanese contractors Mitsui.
facts.quote: In 1979, President J. R. Jayewardene invited Bawa to design Sri Lanka's new Parliament building at Kotte. The project was completed in 1982 with the help of a firm of Japanese contractors, Mitsui.

facts.fact: The site is Duwa, a 5-hectare island about 16 km east of Colombo.
facts.quote: On 4 July 1979, then Prime Minister Ranasinghe Premadasa obtained sanction from Parliament to construct a new Parliament Building at Duwa, a 5 hectares (12 acres) island in the Diyawanna Oya (off Baddegana Road, Pita Sri Jayawardenapura-Kotte) about 16 kilometres (9.9 mi) east of Colombo.

facts.fact: It was built in 26 months and opened on 29 April 1982.
facts.quote: The project was completed on a scheduled time of 26 months. It was officially opened on 29 April 1982 by then President J. R. Jayewardene.

facts.fact: The building is regional modernism: modernist, yet respectful of Sri Lankan vernacular architecture.
facts.quote: The building is designed in a style of regional modernism. While the building is an example of Modernism, it still respects Sri Lankan vernacular architecture.

facts.fact: The complex suggests symmetry, in contrast with the organic form of the lake around it.
facts.quote: The parliament complex has the allusion of symmetry, which contrasts sharply with the organic form of the lake it is located in.

facts.fact: In 1983 it won a Pacific Area Travel Association award for design in the tradition of local vernacular architecture.
facts.quote: Heritage Award of Recognition, for "Outstanding Architectural Design in the Tradition of Local Vernacular Architecture", for the new Parliamentary Complex at Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte from the Pacific Area Travel Association. (1983)

facts.fact: The 270-metre Tabiat Bridge is Tehran's largest pedestrian overpass, linking Taleghani Park and Abo-Atash Park over the Modarres Expressway.
facts.quote: The 270-metre (890 ft) bridge connects two public parks — Taleghani Park and Abo-Atash Park — by spanning  Modarres Expressway, one of the main highways in northern Tehran.

facts.fact: Leila Araghian's design won a local competition, and she wanted a bridge to stay on, so it is not straight and has benches and seating.
facts.quote: In designing the bridge, a process which took a total of 4 years, Araghian wanted it to "be a place for people to stay and ponder, not simply pass." To achieve this, the bridge is not straight and contains benches and seating.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2010 and used 2,000 tonnes of steel and 10,000 cubic metres of concrete; it was finished in October 2014.
facts.quote: Construction of the bridge started in 2010, using a total of 2000 tonnes of steel and 10000 cubic metres of concrete before it was finished in October 2014.

facts.fact: Three tree-shaped columns carry two continuous decks, so the lower level is covered for all seasons; a third level sits where truss meets branches.
facts.quote: Three tree-shaped columns support two continuous deck levels, which makes the lower level covered and suitable for use in all seasons. A third level is located where the truss meets the column branches.

facts.fact: The steel structure is a three-dimensional truss with a curved surface of varying width.
facts.quote: The complex steel structure has a dynamic three-dimensional truss[1] and the surface is curved with a varying width.

facts.fact: Restaurants sit at each end, with seating and kiosks between, and openings let trees grow through.
facts.quote: Restaurants serve customers at either end of the bridge with seating areas and kiosks between. Some areas of the bridge are open to allow trees to grow and the bridge itself has green spaces to encourage visitors to linger.

facts.fact: It won the 2016 Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
facts.quote: The bridge also won the 2016 Aga Khan Award for Architecture for its exemplary approach to an infrastructure project, "a breath of fresh air" according to the award jury.

facts.fact: Four million people visited it in its first year.
facts.quote: Four million people visited the bridge the first year it was open.

facts.fact: The Shah Mosque was begun in 1611 under Abbas the Great and completed around 1630.
facts.quote: Its construction began in 1611, during the Safavid Empire under the order of Abbas the Great, and was completed c. 1630.

facts.fact: Architect Ali Akbar Isfahani is named in the main foundation inscription above the entrance iwan.
facts.quote: The name of the architect Ali Akbar Isfahani appears in the main foundation inscription of the mosque, located above the doorway of the entrance iwan.

facts.fact: Because the square does not face Mecca, the vestibule turns about 45 degrees so the rest of the mosque is aligned for prayer.
facts.quote: Because the square is not aligned with the qibla (the direction of Mecca), the mosque's large vestibule makes an approximately 45-degree turn towards the southwest to allow the rest of the building to follow the correct alignment for prayers.

facts.fact: It uses the four-iwan plan common to Iranian congregational mosques.
facts.quote: It employs the four-iwan plan that was common for Iranian congregational mosques.

facts.fact: The prayer hall dome is 52 metres high and about 25 metres across.
facts.quote: The main prayer hall is covered by a huge dome reaching to a height of 52 metres (171 ft) and a diameter of around 25 metres (82 ft).

facts.fact: The dome is double-shelled, after Timurid domes, with 14 metres between the shells.
facts.quote: It has a double-shelled structure, inspired by earlier Timurid domes, with a difference of 14 metres (46 ft) between the two shells.

facts.fact: The mosque used the new haft rangi (seven-colour) tilework.
facts.quote: The mosque employed the new haft rangi ('seven-colour') style of tilework.

facts.fact: It is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site with Naqsh-e Jahan Square.
facts.quote: The mosque is registered, along with the Naghsh-e Jahan Square and other surrounding structures, as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: Preston Scott Cohen won the Herta and Paul Amir Competition for a new Tel Aviv Museum of Art building in January 2004.
facts.quote: In January 2004, Cohen was the winner of the Herta and Paul Amir Competition to design a new building for the Tel Aviv Museum of Art (estimated $45 million budget to build flexible gallery spaces, concessions, as well as the restoration of labs and offices).

facts.fact: The building is noted for its hyperboloid form and was to be finished in Israeli stone.
facts.quote: The building is noted for its hyperboloid form, and is to be finished with Israeli stone.

facts.fact: It opened on the western side of the museum in November 2011.
facts.quote: In November 2011, the Herta and Paul Amir Building on the western side of the museum opened.

facts.fact: It houses an Israeli Architecture Archive and a new section of photography and visual arts.
facts.quote: It houses an Israeli Architecture Archive, and a new section of Photography and Visual arts.

facts.fact: The wing holds 18,500 square feet of galleries over five floors.
facts.quote: The new wing houses 18,500 square feet of gallery space over five floors.

facts.fact: Renderings of the project were shown in the Skin + Bones exhibition at MOCA, Los Angeles, in 2006–2007.
facts.quote: Renderings of the project were shown at the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles in a 2006-2007 exhibition entitled Skin + Bones: parallel practices in fashion and architecture.

facts.fact: Heneghan Peng's Palestinian Museum opened in May 2016.
facts.quote: The Palestinian Museum, Palestine, May 2016

facts.fact: The design won the 2019 Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
facts.quote: 2019 Aga Khan Award for Architecture for their design of the Palestinian Museum.

facts.fact: The fairground in Tripoli is a complex of buildings by Oscar Niemeyer, commissioned in 1962.
facts.quote: The International Fair of Tripoli site, formally known as the Rachid Karami International Exhibition Center, is a complex of buildings designed by the Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer who was commissioned for the project in 1962.

facts.fact: It was built for a World's Fair, but work stopped in 1975 when the Lebanese civil war broke out, and never resumed.
facts.quote: The site was built for a World's Fair event to be held in the city, but construction was halted in 1975 due to the outbreak of the Lebanese civil war, and never resumed.

facts.fact: The site holds 15 partly completed Niemeyer buildings on about 75.6 hectares.
facts.quote: The site contains 15 partly-completed Niemeyer buildings within an approximate 75.6 ha (187-acre) area near Tripoli's southern entrance.

facts.fact: In 2023 it was added to the World Heritage List and the List of World Heritage in Danger.
facts.quote: In 2023, the Rashid Karami International Fair was added to both the World Heritage List and the List of World Heritage in Danger.

facts.fact: The university was founded in 1948 as University College Ibadan, a branch of the University of London, which awarded its degrees until 1967.
facts.quote: The university was established in 1948 as University College Ibadan, a branch of the University of London, which supervised its academic programs and awarded degrees until 1967.

facts.fact: It was Nigeria's first degree-awarding institution.
facts.quote: However, the limited aims of Yaba College and clamor by Nigerian nationalists for self-improvement and uninhibited education led to the establishment of University College Ibadan as the first degree-awarding institution in Nigeria in 1948.

facts.fact: The first sod on the permanent site was cut on 17 November 1948, now Founders' Day.
facts.quote: The sod of its permanent site was cut on 17 November 1948, a date now known as its Founders' Day.

facts.fact: The first buildings were designed by the modernist architects Maxwell Fry and Jane Drew.
facts.quote: The university's first buildings were designed by eminent modernist architects Maxwell Fry and Jane Drew.

facts.fact: Fry's work on the university ran from 1949 to 1960.
facts.quote: 1949–60 University of Ibadan, Nigeria

facts.fact: The Times considered the University of Ibadan Fry's most notable work in West Africa.
facts.quote: The Times considered Fry's most notable work in West Africa to be the University of Ibadan.

facts.fact: The university has 15 halls of residence.
facts.quote: The University of Ibadan has 15 halls of residence that provide accommodation for about 30% of the population of students in the regular studies mode.

facts.fact: The Shard is a 95-storey mixed-use pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Southwark, London, designed by Renzo Piano.
facts.quote: The Shard, also referred to as the Shard London Bridge and formerly London Bridge Tower, is a 95-storey mixed-use development supertall pyramid-shaped skyscraper, designed by the Italian architect Renzo Piano, in Southwark, London, that forms part of The Shard Quarter development.

facts.fact: At 309.6 metres it is the tallest building in the United Kingdom and Western Europe.
facts.quote: Standing 309.6 metres (1,016 feet) high, The Shard is the tallest building in the United Kingdom and Western Europe; and the seventh-tallest building in Europe.

facts.fact: Construction began in March 2009, and the tower was inaugurated on 5 July 2012.
facts.quote: The Shard's construction began in March 2009; it was topped out on 30 March 2012 and inaugurated on 5 July 2012.

facts.fact: Piano designed it as a spire-like sculpture rising from the Thames, inspired by the railway lines, Canaletto's London spires and the masts of sailing ships.
facts.quote: Renzo Piano, the project's architect, designed The Shard as a spire-like sculpture emerging from the River Thames. He was inspired by the railway lines next to the site, the London spires depicted by the 18th-century Venetian painter Canaletto, and the masts of sailing ships.

facts.fact: The name came from English Heritage's criticism that it would be 'a shard of glass through the heart of historic London'.
facts.quote: Piano's design met criticism from English Heritage, who claimed the building would be "a shard of glass through the heart of historic London", giving the building its name, The Shard.

facts.fact: Its angled glass panes reflect sunlight and sky, so the building's look changes with weather and season.
facts.quote: He proposed a sophisticated use of glazing, with expressive façades of angled glass panes intended to reflect sunlight and the sky above, so that the appearance of the building would change according to the weather and seasons.

facts.fact: It was built top-down, digging foundations while the core rose, a first for the UK.
facts.quote: For the construction of the skyscraper some path-breaking engineering methods were used, such as top-down construction, where foundations are dug while the core is built up – this was a first for the UK.

facts.fact: It stacks a 26-floor office complex, three restaurants, the Shangri-La hotel, 10 apartments and a viewing gallery.
facts.quote: The Shard comprises a 26-floor office complex, occupied by 32 companies across 10 business sectors, 3 restaurants—Aqua Shard, Oblix, and Hutong—the five-star Shangri-La The Shard, London hotel, 10 residential apartments, and the UK's highest viewing gallery, The View from The Shard.

facts.fact: The New York Times Building is a 52-story skyscraper at 620 Eighth Avenue near Times Square, Manhattan.
facts.quote: The New York Times Building is a 52-story skyscraper at 620 Eighth Avenue, between 40th and 41st Streets near Times Square, on the west side of Midtown Manhattan in New York City, New York, U.S.

facts.fact: It was Renzo Piano's first design in New York City, made with Fox & Fowle.
facts.quote: The New York Times Building was designed by Renzo Piano and Fox & Fowle and was developed by the New York Times Company, Forest City Ratner, and ING Real Estate. It was Piano's first design in New York City.

facts.fact: Piano and Fox & Fowle were chosen through a design competition; the building was completed in 2007 for over $1 billion.
facts.quote: Piano and Fox & Fowle were selected following an architectural design competition, and the land was acquired in 2003 following disputes with existing landowners. The building was completed in 2007 for over $1 billion.

facts.fact: The plan is cruciform, with a steel frame and a braced mechanical core.
facts.quote: The building is cruciform in plan and has a steel-framed superstructure with a braced mechanical core.

facts.fact: About 186,000 ceramic rods, which the architects called 'baguettes', screen the facade.
facts.quote: There are about 186,000 ceramic rods on the building's facade, which the architects referred to as "baguettes".

facts.fact: The rods deflect heat and glare even without tinted glass, and change colour with sun and weather.
facts.quote: The rods are intended to deflect heat and glare even if the glass panes were not tinted, and they can change color with the sun and weather.

facts.fact: Floor-to-ceiling glass was meant to signify the transparency of the media and to bring in natural light.
facts.quote: The use of floor-to-ceiling glass was meant to signify the transparency of the media. It also maximizes natural light and the physical transparency of the facade.

facts.fact: The notched corners expose their steel, a feature that stands for journalistic transparency.
facts.quote: The notched corners contain exposed steel and lack screens, a design feature that represents the ideal of journalistic transparency.

facts.fact: Turning Torso is a residential skyscraper in Malmö, built in 2005.
facts.quote: Turning Torso is a neo-futurist residential skyscraper built in Malmö, Sweden, in 2005.

facts.fact: Santiago Calatrava designed it, and it opened on 27 August 2005.
facts.quote: It was designed by Spanish architect, structural engineer, sculptor and painter Santiago Calatrava and officially opened on 27 August 2005.

facts.fact: It rises 190 metres with 54 storeys and 147 apartments.
facts.quote: It reaches a height of 190 m (620 ft) with 54 stories and 147 apartments.

facts.fact: The design is based on Calatrava's marble sculpture Twisting Torso, modelled on a twisting human body.
facts.quote: Turning Torso is based on Twisting Torso, a white marble sculpture by Calatrava that was based on the form of a twisting human being.

facts.fact: It is built in nine five-storey segments that twist as it rises, the top one turned 90 degrees from the ground floor.
facts.quote: It is a solid, immobile building constructed in nine segments of five-story pentagons that twist relative to each other as it rises; the topmost segment is twisted 90 degrees clockwise from the ground floor.

facts.fact: Each pentagonal floor rotates around a vertical core supported by an exterior steel framework.
facts.quote: Each floor consists of an irregular pentagonal shape rotating around the vertical core, which is supported by an exterior steel framework.

facts.fact: It was meant to give Malmö a new landmark after the Kockums shipbuilding crane was removed in 2002.
facts.quote: One reason for building Turning Torso was to re-establish a recognisable skyline for Malmö since the removal in 2002 of the Kockums Crane, which was located less than one kilometre (0.6 mi) from Turning Torso.

facts.fact: It won the 2005 Gold Emporis Skyscraper Award.
facts.quote: Turning Torso won the 2005 Gold Emporis Skyscraper Award; and in 2015, the 10 Year Award from the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat.

facts.fact: The museum, designed by Jean Nouvel, shows the indigenous art and cultures of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas.
facts.quote: The museum, designed by French architect Jean Nouvel, features the indigenous art and cultures of Africa, Asia, Oceania, and the Americas.

facts.fact: Nouvel won an international competition held in 1999.
facts.quote: At the beginning of 1999 a jury was formed and an international competition was held to select an architect.

facts.fact: To suit its neighbours, the main building sits lower than those around it and is partly screened by gardens, following the curve of the Seine.
facts.quote: The new museum was designed to correspond to the adjacent buildings as much as possible; the main building appears lower than the buildings around it and is partially screened from view by its gardens. The shape of the main building follows the curve of the Seine, and the three administrative buildings are constructed to harmonize with the Haussmann-period buildings next to them.

facts.fact: The gallery building spans like a bridge 10 metres over the garden, on two concrete silos and 26 steel columns.
facts.quote: It is constructed like a huge bridge, 10 meters over the garden, supported by two large concrete silos at the east and west ends and by 26 steel columns.

facts.fact: Thirty galleries on the north side show on the outside as boxes of different colours.
facts.quote: Thirty different galleries are placed on the north side, which are visible on the outside of the structure as boxes of different colours.

facts.fact: Inside, galleries have no walls, barriers or railings between the four continents.
facts.quote: Nouvel designed the interior of the museum in such a way as to liberate artifacts from the traditional design of museums by not including walls, barriers and railings in the gallery spaces.

facts.fact: Gilles Clément's gardens are the opposite of a formal French garden, with no fences, lawn or gates.
facts.quote: They were designed by landscape architect Gilles Clément, and present the exact opposite of a traditional French formal garden: There are no fences, no lawn, no gates, no monumental stairway; instead, Clément composed a tapestry of small gardens, with streams, hills, pools, and groves, using the native French plants and imported plants accustomed to the Paris climate.

facts.fact: Botanist Patrick Blanc made the green wall, which covers 800 square metres of the facades.
facts.quote: Another notable feature of the Museum garden is the green wall, or wall of vegetation, created by botanist Patrick Blanc. This living wall of greenery covers 800 m2 of the façades of the museum, and 150 m2 of the interior walls.

facts.fact: A high double wall of plate glass shields the garden from the street along the Seine.
facts.quote: On the north side, facing the street along the Seine, the garden is protected by a high double wall of plate glass, which blocks most of the sound from the street.

facts.fact: The mosque is the seat of the Italian Islamic Cultural Centre.
facts.quote: It is also the seat of the Italian Islamic Cultural Centre (Italian: Centro Culturale Islamico d'Italia).

facts.fact: With 30,000 square metres of land, it is the largest mosque in the Western world and holds more than 12,000 worshippers.
facts.quote: With a land area of 30,000 square metres (320,000 sq ft), it is the largest mosque in the Western world and can accommodate more than 12,000 worshipers.

facts.fact: It was designed by Paolo Portoghesi, Vittorio Gigliotti and Sami Mousawi.
facts.quote: The project was designed and directed by Paolo Portoghesi, Vittorio Gigliotti and Sami Mousawi.

facts.fact: The land was donated in 1974, the first stone laid in 1984, and the mosque inaugurated on 21 June 1995.
facts.quote: Its planning took more than ten years: the Roman City Council donated the land in 1974, but the first stone was laid only in 1984, in the presence of then President of the Italian Republic Sandro Pertini, with its inauguration on 21 June 1995.

facts.fact: The minaret was kept about a metre below the dome of St Peter's.
facts.quote: In the end, the issue was resolved by shortening the height of the minaret slightly to be below that of the dome of St Peter's by approximately one meter (3.3 ft).

facts.fact: Travertine and terracotta evoke traditional Roman building, and light and shade are blended for a meditative mood.
facts.quote: Lights and shades are blended in a manner intended to create a meditative climate, and the choice of materials, like travertino and cotto, evoke traditional Roman architectural styles.

facts.fact: The prayer hall has a central dome over 20 metres high, surrounded by 16 smaller domes.
facts.quote: The main prayer hall is topped by a central dome over 20 metres (66 ft) high, which is surrounded by 16 smaller domes.

facts.fact: Its palm-shaped columns represent the connection between God and the single worshipper.
facts.quote: The mosque contains several palm-shaped columns, which represent the connection between God and the single devotee.

facts.fact: La Seine Musicale is a music and performing arts centre on Île Seguin, an island in the Seine west of Paris.
facts.quote: La Seine Musicale (French pronunciation: [la sɛn myzikal]; lit. 'The Musical Seine') is a music and performing arts center located on Île Seguin an island on the Seine river between Boulogne-Billancourt and Sèvres, in the western suburbs of Paris, France.

facts.fact: It was designed by Shigeru Ban and Jean de Gastines and opened in April 2017.
facts.quote: The initial complex of buildings on the island opened in April 2017 and were designed by the architectural team of Shigeru Ban and Jean de Gastines.

facts.fact: It holds a raised egg-shaped theatre-in-the-round, a larger concert hall, rehearsal rooms and a large roof garden.
facts.quote: The facilities include an elevated egg-shaped theater-in-the-round mostly for classical music, a larger concert hall that hosts pop stars, rehearsal rooms for musicians (Riffx Studios), seminar rooms, a press center, restaurants and an extensive roof garden.

facts.fact: A large movable curved solar array over the smaller auditorium supplies much of its daytime energy.
facts.quote: Much of the site's daytime energy needs are supplied by a large mobile curved solar panel array that covers the smaller auditorium.

facts.fact: The auditorium seats 1,150, and the Grande Seine hall holds up to 6,000.
facts.quote: Seating capacity for the unamplified Patrick-Devedjian Auditorium is 1,150. The larger modular concert hall, Grande Seine, at a lower elevation on the island site, is able to accommodate audiences of up to 6,000.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 22 April 2017.
facts.quote: La Seine Musicale was inaugurated on 22 April 2017 with a concert by Insula orchestra, accompanied by the Accentus choir, conducted by Laurence Equilbey at the Patrick Devedjian Auditorium.

facts.fact: The Palace is a 62-metre pyramid in Astana that serves as a non-denominational national spiritual centre and event venue.
facts.quote: The Palace of Peace and Reconciliation (Kazakh: Бейбітшілік пен келісім сарайы, Beibıtşılık pen kelısım saraiy), also translated as the Pyramid of Peace and Accord, is a 62-metre-high (203 ft) pyramid in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, that serves as a non-denominational national spiritual centre and event venue.

facts.fact: It was built for the triennial Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions and completed in 2006.
facts.quote: The Palace was constructed to house the triennial Congress of Leaders of World and Traditional Religions, and completed in 2006.

facts.fact: The pyramid sits on a 15-metre earth-covered block.
facts.quote: The pyramidical portion of the building is 62 metres high and sits on a 15-metre-high (49 ft)  earth-covered block.

facts.fact: The lower three rows of triangles are clad in pale granite.
facts.quote: The lower portion, made of three "stories" of triangles, is clad in pale granite.

facts.fact: The pyramid has a steel frame, with concrete for the lower levels.
facts.quote: Construction is of a steel frame for the pyramid structure, and concrete for the lower levels.

facts.fact: To cope with temperature swings, one corner is fixed and the other three sit on bridge bearings, used in a building for the first time.
facts.quote: Due to the extreme climate of the city, the engineers locked down one corner of the pyramid, and placed the three other corners on bridge bearings, a common technique for building bridges, but used in a building for the first time.

facts.fact: It also holds a 1,300-seat opera house, a national museum of culture and a library.
facts.quote: It also houses a 1,300-seat opera house, a national museum of culture, a new "university of civilization", a library and a research center for Kazakhstan's ethnic and geographical groups.

facts.fact: Delegates meet under the glass in a circular chamber based on the UN Security Council room.
facts.quote: Bathed in the golden and pale blue glow of the stained glass (colors taken from the Kazakhstan flag), 200 delegates from the world's main religions and faith meet every three years in a circular chamber based on the United Nations Security Council meeting room in New York.

facts.fact: The ECB's seat in Frankfurt combines a twin-tower skyscraper with the former Wholesale Market Hall, linked by a low-rise building.
facts.quote: Its premises comprise a twin-tower skyscraper and the city's former Wholesale Market Hall (Großmarkthalle), with a low-rise building connecting the two.

facts.fact: Coop Himmelb(l)au won the international competition launched in 1999.
facts.quote: In 1999, an international architectural competition was launched by the bank to design a new building. It was won by a Vienna-based architectural office called Coop Himmelb(l)au.

facts.fact: The two towers are joined by an atrium with four interchange platforms.
facts.quote: The main office building, constructed for the ECB, consists of two towers that are joined by an atrium with four interchange platforms.

facts.fact: The North tower has 45 storeys and rises 185 metres; the South tower has 43 storeys and 165 metres.
facts.quote: The North tower has 45 storeys and a roof height of 185 m (607 ft), whereas the South tower has 43 storeys and a roof height of 165 m (541 ft).

facts.fact: The market hall, built in 1926–28 for the New Frankfurt project, was fully renovated for its new use.
facts.quote: The ECB premises also includes the Grossmarkthalle, a former wholesale market hall built from 1926 to 1928 as part of the New Frankfurt project and the world's widest monocoque construction at the time, fully renovated for its new purpose.

facts.fact: It was completed in 2014 and officially opened on 18 March 2015.
facts.quote: It was completed in 2014 and was officially opened on 18 March 2015.

facts.fact: The project cost between 1.3 and 1.4 billion euros.
facts.quote: The total cost of the project was between 1.3 and 1.4 billion euros.

facts.fact: The library stands on Centenary Square, beside the Birmingham Rep, which it connects to.
facts.quote: It is situated on the west side of the city centre at Centenary Square, beside the Birmingham Rep (to which it connects, and with which it shares some facilities) and Baskerville House.

facts.fact: It opened on 3 September 2013, replacing Birmingham Central Library.
facts.quote: Upon opening on 3 September 2013, it replaced Birmingham Central Library.

facts.fact: Mecanoo, with engineers Buro Happold, won the design competition in August 2008.
facts.quote: In early August 2008, Mecanoo and multi-discipline engineers, Buro Happold, were announced as the winner of the design competition.

facts.fact: It has been described as the largest public library in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: It has been described as the largest public library in the United Kingdom, the largest public cultural space in Europe, and the largest regional library in Europe.

facts.fact: An aquifer ground-source system pumps cold groundwater into the air conditioning to cut energy use.
facts.quote: The library uses an aquifer ground source system to reduce energy consumption. Cold groundwater is pumped up from within the earth and used in the air conditioning system.

facts.fact: The 1882 Shakespeare Memorial Room by John Henry Chamberlain was moved again, to the top floor.
facts.quote: When the Library of Birmingham was built, it was again moved, to the top floor.

facts.fact: It was shortlisted for the 2014 Stirling Prize.
facts.quote: On 17 July 2014 the Library of Birmingham was nominated as one of the six short-listed buildings for the 2014 Stirling Prize, awarded for excellence in architecture.

facts.fact: Marina Bay Sands is an integrated resort on Marina Bay with a 1,850-room hotel, convention centre, mall, museum, theatre and casino.
facts.quote: The resort includes a 1,850-room hotel, a 120,000-square-metre (1,300,000 sq ft) meetings and conventions facility at Sands Expo & Convention Centre, a 74,000-square-metre (800,000 sq ft) luxury shopping mall, The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, an ArtScience museum, a 2,183-capacity theatre, the world's first floating Apple store, the world's first Louis Vuitton Island Maison, celebrity chef, signature and Michelin-starred restaurants, and a casino with 500 tables and 3,000 electronic gaming machines.

facts.fact: The 20-hectare resort was designed by Moshe Safdie.
facts.quote: The 20-hectare resort was designed by Moshe Safdie.

facts.fact: Safdie says the design was first inspired by card decks.
facts.quote: The resort is designed by Moshe Safdie, who says it was initially inspired by card decks.

facts.fact: The towers are broader at the base and narrow as they rise, each with two asymmetric legs, one curved and leaning on the other.
facts.quote: The three towers are broader at the base and narrow as they rise. Each tower has two asymmetric legs, with a curved eastern leg leaning against the other, creating a significant technical challenge in its construction.

facts.fact: The 340-metre Sands SkyPark links the three towers and overhangs the north tower by 66.5 metres.
facts.quote: The complex includes three towers topped by the Sands Skypark, a 340-metre-long (1,120 ft) skyway connecting the towers with a capacity of 3,902 people and a 150 m (490 ft) infinity swimming pool, set on top of the world's largest public cantilevered platform, which overhangs the north tower by 66.5 m (218 ft).

facts.fact: The SkyPark hull was prefabricated in 14 steel sections and assembled on top of the towers.
facts.quote: The hull of the SkyPark was pre-fabricated off-site in 14 separate steel sections and then assembled on top of the towers.

facts.fact: It is the sixth building on Museum Island, on the site of Schinkel's former Packhof.
facts.quote: As the sixth building on Museum Island, the gallery has a prominent position at the site of the former Packhof designed by Karl Friedrich Schinkel, which was demolished in 1938, and its design is inspired by the construction history of Museum Island.

facts.fact: Like the Louvre Pyramid, it receives visitors to the island and directs them to the exhibits.
facts.quote: Similar in function to the Louvre Pyramid, the James Simon Gallery is designed to receive the visitors for the island, offer them orientation, and direct them to the exhibits featured on the main circuit.

facts.fact: A broad stair leads to a raised plateau with 70 white concrete columns almost nine metres tall and under 30 cm thick.
facts.quote: A broad staircase leads up in three flights to an elevated plateau with a line of 70 white concrete columns that stand almost nine metres high but are less than 30 centimetres thick.

facts.fact: The revised 2007 design set a stone base framed by a modern continuation of Stüler's colonnades.
facts.quote: The design of the reception building consisted of a stone basement, framed by a modern continuation of Friedrich August Stüler's colonnades at the Alte Nationalgalerie.

facts.fact: It completes the master plan Chipperfield drew up for Museum Island in 1999.
facts.quote: The James Simon Gallery was developed as the final piece of a master plan which Chipperfield conceived for Berlin's Museum Island in 1999.

facts.fact: It holds a 300-seat auditorium with pleated concrete acoustic walls, a temporary exhibition space and cafés for the whole island.
facts.quote: The building provides a 300-seat auditorium, with concrete walls cast in pleated acoustic folds; a media centre; a 600-square metre space for temporary exhibitions; a bookstore; shops; cafés and restaurants for all of Museum Island.

facts.fact: It is named after the art patron Henri James Simon.
facts.quote: The gallery is named in honour of the art patron Henri James Simon (1851–1932) who brought worldwide fame to the Berlin State Museums with his lavish donations, including important artwork and artifacts.

facts.fact: IWM North, one of five branches of the Imperial War Museum, explores the impact of modern conflict on people and society.
facts.quote: One of five branches of the Imperial War Museum, it explores the impact of modern conflicts on people and society.

facts.fact: It overlooks the Manchester Ship Canal in Trafford Park, a wartime industrial area heavily bombed in the 1940 Blitz.
facts.quote: The museum occupies a site overlooking the Manchester Ship Canal on Trafford Wharf Road, Trafford Park, an area which during World War II was a key industrial centre and consequently heavily bombed during the Manchester Blitz in 1940.

facts.fact: Daniel Libeskind won the 1997 architectural competition.
facts.quote: An architectural competition for the new museum was held in 1997, with the winning design being that of Berlin-based architect Daniel Libeskind.

facts.fact: Libeskind imagined three interlocking shards, each a remnant of a globe shattered by conflict.
facts.quote: Libeskind envisaged a 'constellation composed of three interlocking shards'  with each shard being a remnant of an imagined globe shattered by conflict.

facts.fact: The shards stand for air, earth and water, and each holds a different part of the museum.
facts.quote: These shards in turn represented air, earth and water, and each formed a functionally distinct part of the museum.

facts.fact: The 55-metre air shard is the entrance and once held a viewing balcony over the canal.
facts.quote: The 55 m high air shard, provides the museum's entranceway and a viewing balcony (now closed to the public) above the Manchester Ship Canal with views of the Manchester skyline.

facts.fact: The gallery floor in the earth shard curves away like the curvature of the Earth.
facts.quote: As part of the earth shard, the 3,500 m2 floor of the gallery is curved, gradually dropping away like the curvature of the Earth from a nominal "North Pole" near the gallery's entrance.

facts.fact: Budget cuts replaced concrete with metal for the shards and removed a planned auditorium.
facts.quote: The reduction in budget forced a number of changes; the substitution of metal for concrete in the construction of the shards, the removal of a planned auditorium, and a change of exhibition content.

facts.fact: The Royal Danish Playhouse is a theatre building for the Royal Danish Theatre in central Copenhagen.
facts.quote: The Royal Danish Playhouse (Danish: Skuespilhuset) is a theatre building for the Royal Danish Theatre in central Copenhagen, Denmark.

facts.fact: It was built as a purpose-built venue for drama, alongside the 1874 theatre and the 2004 Opera House.
facts.quote: It was created as a purpose-built venue for dramatic theatre, supplementing the theatre's old venue from 1874 on Kongens Nytorv and the 2004 Copenhagen Opera House, which are used for ballet and opera.

facts.fact: It is built of a long, slim, deep-brown brick developed specially for the project.
facts.quote: It is built in a long, slim, deep-brown brick that was specially developed for the project.

facts.fact: A glass-encased top storey holds offices and backstage rooms, under the copper-clad cube of the stage tower.
facts.quote: The exterior is dominated by a continuous glass-encased top story with offices and back-stage facilities for the actors. Above the glass band is the dark copper-clad cube of the stage tower.

facts.fact: A glazed foyer runs the full length of the building, facing the harbour.
facts.quote: The glazed foyer facing the water runs along the entire length of the building.

facts.fact: About 40 percent of the building projects over the water, and a raised 150-metre oak walkway on crooked columns carries the promenade around it.
facts.quote: With about 40 per cent of the building projecting over the water, the waterfront promenade pivots around the playhouse, diverting pedestrians onto a raised 150 metre long walkway layered with rustic oak planks placed on Venetian-style crooked columns creating a floating feel.

facts.fact: It won a RIBA European Award in 2008.
facts.quote: The building received a RIBA European Award in 2008 for its architecture as well as a Red dot design award for the design of the chairs.

facts.fact: Kulturhuset is a cultural centre on the south side of Sergels torg in central Stockholm.
facts.quote: House of Culture (Swedish: Kulturhuset) is a cultural center on the south side of Sergels torg in central Stockholm, Sweden.

facts.fact: Peter Celsing won the 1965 architectural competition.
facts.quote: In 1965 the city's government announced an architectural competition won by modernist architect Peter Celsing (1920–1974).

facts.fact: Begun in 1966 and inaugurated in 1974, its glass front and thin concrete floors look like open shelves facing Sergels torg.
facts.quote: The cultural center Kulturhuset (begun 1966, inaugurated 1974; the western part including the theatre was completed in 1971) is from most angles dominated by its concrete structure, with the adjacent theatre building having a façade of stainless steel, but from the front by its glass façade and the thin lines of the concrete floors, giving the impression of a number of shelves open towards the open place outside, Sergels torg.

facts.fact: It was meant as a 'cultural oasis' in a new commercial centre, with an open library, a theatre and exhibition space.
facts.quote: Kulturhuset was intended as a "cultural oasis" in this new city of commerce, with an open library in the bottom floor, a large theatre, and space for exhibitions in the rest of the building; the original intention was for the Stockholm Museum of Modern Art to occupy large parts of the building, but the museum dropped out of the project in 1969.

facts.fact: It served as the temporary seat of the Swedish parliament until 1983.
facts.quote: Kulturhuset was the temporary seat of the Riksdag, the Swedish Parliament, until 1983, while the Riksdag building was remodelled for a unicameral legislature, which had been introduced in Sweden 1971.

facts.fact: It won the Kasper Salin Prize in 1972.
facts.quote: The public opinion against the project may have been strengthened by the fact that the Kulturhuset and the interconnected Stockholm City Theatre were used as a temporary parliamentary building for several years, but as such the structure won the prestigious Kasper Salin Prize in 1972.

facts.fact: It has been described as a symbol of Stockholm and of the growth of modernism in Sweden.
facts.quote: The House of Culture has been described as a symbol for Stockholm as well as of the growth of modernism in Sweden.

facts.fact: Arne Jacobsen designed the hotel for Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS).
facts.quote: The hotel was designed by Danish architect and designer Arne Jacobsen for the airline Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS).

facts.fact: It opened on 1 July 1960 as the Royal Hotel.
facts.quote: It was opened on July 1, 1960, by King Frederik IX and Queen Ingrid as the Royal Hotel.

facts.fact: At 69.6 metres it was Copenhagen's first skyscraper and Denmark's tallest building until 1969.
facts.quote: At 69.60 meters in height, it was the first skyscraper in Copenhagen, and until 1969, the tallest high-rise building in Denmark.

facts.fact: Jacobsen designed everything, from building and furniture to fittings, and it has been called the world's first designer hotel.
facts.quote: With the SAS Royal Hotel, built from 1956 to 1960, Jacobsen was given the opportunity to design what has been called "the world's first designer hotel." He designed everything from the building and its furniture and fittings to the ashtrays sold in the souvenir shop and the airport buses.

facts.fact: The Egg and Swan chairs were created for the hotel.
facts.quote: Two other successful chair designs, the Egg and the Swan, were created for the SAS Royal Hotel which he also designed in 1956.

facts.fact: Its form follows Lever House: a two-storey base supports a tall 'punch card' tower.
facts.quote: The building's sense of lightness emanates from its Lever House-inspired form with a two-story base supporting its lofty "punch card" tower.

facts.fact: The tower is a reinforced concrete frame with a curtain wall of aluminium and green and grey glass.
facts.quote: The reinforced concrete frame structure erected in the tower has a curtain wall of aluminum profiles and transparent green and gray anodized glass.

facts.fact: Only room 606 keeps its original green furniture and wood panelling.
facts.quote: Only a single room has been kept in the original design. It has all of the original, green furniture and the wood panels on the wall.

facts.fact: Flamengo Park, by Roberto Burle Marx, is a large public park in Rio de Janeiro built on landfill.
facts.quote: Flamengo Park – large public park in Rio de Janeiro built on landfill

facts.fact: MARCO is in central Monterrey, next to the Macroplaza and the Barrio Antiguo district.
facts.quote: The museum is in the Centro district of Monterrey, adjacent to the Macroplaza and to the Barrio Antiguo district.

facts.fact: Ricardo Legorreta designed it in a minimalist post-modern style, and it opened in 1991.
facts.quote: MARCO was designed by Mexican architect Ricardo Legorreta, in a Minimalist Post-modern architectural style. The museum building opened in 1991.

facts.fact: Artworks are shown in a balance of natural and artificial light.
facts.quote: The artworks are in spaces with balanced arrangements of natural and artificial light.

facts.fact: The 16,000 m² building has 5,000 m² of exhibition space in 11 galleries.
facts.quote: The museum occupies a 16,000-square-metre (170,000 sq ft) structure, with 5,000 square metres (54,000 sq ft) for exhibitions in 11 gallery halls.

facts.fact: It has a sculpture garden and a Central Patio with a water-mirror fountain.
facts.quote: There is an outdoor sculpture garden courtyard, the Central Patio courtyard with a water mirror fountain, and an auditorium, gift shop and restaurant.

facts.fact: Juan Soriano's bronze dove, La Paloma, marks the entrance plaza.
facts.quote: It is an abstracted dove, titled "La Paloma" (the dove), by sculptor Juan Soriano.

facts.fact: The Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, the 'New Cathedral', is in Managua, Nicaragua.
facts.quote: The Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception of Mary (Spanish: Catedral Metropolitana de la Inmaculada Concepción de María), referred to as the New Cathedral (La Nueva Catedral), is located in Managua, Nicaragua.

facts.fact: It replaced the Old Cathedral, damaged in the 1972 earthquake that destroyed 90% of the city.
facts.quote: The old cathedral was damaged and thought to be unrestoreable after a 1972 earthquake that destroyed 90% of the city.

facts.fact: Ricardo Legorreta designed it; building began around August 1991 and it was inaugurated on 4 September 1993.
facts.quote: The new cathedral was designed by the Mexican architect Ricardo Legorreta. Construction began around August 1991, and the cathedral was inaugurated on September 4, 1993.

facts.fact: It cost an estimated $4.5 million.
facts.quote: The cost of the newly built cathedral was estimated at $4.5 million.

facts.fact: Locals nickname it La Chichona for its many cupolas.
facts.quote: Locals refer to it as La Chichona on account of the plethora of cupolas adorning it which resemble many chichas (Nicaraguan spanish: slang for "breasts").

facts.fact: It is counted among Legorreta's most famous works.
facts.quote: His most famous works are the Camino Real Hotel in Mexico City, the IBM Factory in Guadalajara and the Cathedral of Managua.

facts.fact: The International Museum of the Baroque in Puebla, Mexico, is a museum of Baroque art designed by Toyo Ito.
facts.quote: The International Museum of the Baroque (Spanish: Museo Internacional del Barroco, MIB) is a museum of Baroque art designed by Japanese architect Toyo Ito located in Puebla, Mexico.

facts.fact: It opened on 4 February 2016.
facts.quote: It opened on February 4, 2016.

facts.fact: It was set up to conserve, research and share the many forms of Baroque sensibility, in art, culture, science and technology.
facts.quote: The original MIB project was dedicated to the conservation, research, and dissemination of the diverse manifestations of Baroque sensibility in its artistic, cultural, social, scientific, and technological aspects.

facts.fact: Its first curatorial plan covered Baroque architecture, painting, sculpture and literature, with temporary exhibitions.
facts.quote: The initial curatorial proposal sought to represent the complexity of Baroque expression in the fields of architecture, painting and sculpture, literature, and others; it also included a program of temporary exhibitions.

facts.fact: After controversy over its collection and costs, it reopened on 26 October 2019 under a new state administration.
facts.quote: Following this controversy, and with the change of state administration, the MIB was reopened on October 26, 2019, with the exhibition " New Rites: Saints, Mourning, and Deities" by Mexican artist Mauro Terán.

facts.fact: Lego House is a 12,000 m² visitor centre in Billund, near Legoland and the Lego Group headquarters.
facts.quote: Lego House is a 12,000-square metre building filled with 25 million Lego bricks in Billund, Denmark, located near Legoland and the headquarters of The Lego Group.

facts.fact: Bjarke Ingels Group designed it, and it opened on 28 September 2017.
facts.quote: The house was designed by the Bjarke Ingels Group and was inaugurated on 28 September 2017.

facts.fact: It is designed as a pile of 21 white Lego bricks stacked on each other.
facts.quote: Lego House was designed to resemble a pile of 21 white Lego bricks that have been built on top of each other.

facts.fact: The rooms and the white facade tiles follow the proportions of a classic 2x4 brick.
facts.quote: The modular spaces were built with the exact proportions of a Lego brick, while the white tiles that cover the building also have the proportions of a classic 2x4 brick.

facts.fact: White ceramic tiles on the facade reflect light and keep the outside subdued.
facts.quote: White ceramic tiles were used on the external façade to reflect the light and create a subdued form, in an effort to avoid overloading Billund with too much colour.

facts.fact: To keep the spaces free of columns, the 21 rooms hang from a steel bridge.
facts.quote: In order to achieve unobstructed internal spaces, the 21 modular rooms were hung from a steel bridge.

facts.fact: The roof terraces are free to enter, offering the town a communal urban space.
facts.quote: In addition to its concept as a visitor centre, Lego House was also created to offer a communal urban space to the local community, due to its central location in Billund, with many areas of the complex, such as the roof terraces, having been designed to be entirely free to enter.

facts.fact: It stands on the site of Billund's former town hall, a few metres from the workshop where Lego began in 1932.
facts.quote: The building was constructed on the former site of Billund town hall, just a few metres from the location of the workshop where the company began in 1932.

facts.fact: PAC is on via Palestro in Milan, next to the Galleria d'Arte Moderna and facing the public gardens.
facts.quote: It is on via Palestro, next to the Galleria d'Arte Moderna, and across from the Giardini Pubblici Indro Montanelli.

facts.fact: It was built on the site of Villa Belgioioso, which was bombed in 1943, as a new space just for contemporary art.
facts.quote: In 1947 the Municipality of Milan, pressed by the need to find a new exhibition space for contemporary art, focused its attention on the site of Villa Belgioiosa, destroyed by bombing in 1943.

facts.fact: Ignazio Gardella's design was chosen in March 1948, and the pavilion opened in 1954.
facts.quote: The design by the architect Ignazio Gardella was preliminarily selected in March 1948, and the Pavilion was inaugurated in 1954.

facts.fact: A Mafia bomb destroyed the building in 1993.
facts.quote: In 1993 a bomb destroyed the building (Via Palestro massacre) at a time when Italy was heavily committed in its fight against the Mafia.

facts.fact: Gardella rebuilt it to the original design, with technical improvements.
facts.quote: Gardella subsequently rebuilt the exhibiting space according to the original design, though with key technical improvements.

facts.fact: He rebuilt it with his son Jacopo Gardella in 1996.
facts.quote: 1947-1954 Padiglione d'Arte Contemporanea (PAC), Milan (which he rebuilt with his son Jacopo Gardella in 1996 after the attack of 1993)

facts.fact: Tampere's main municipal library is nicknamed Metso ('Capercaillie') because from above it looks like the bird.
facts.quote: Tampere Central Library (Finnish: Tampereen kaupungin pääkirjasto) is the main municipal library in Tampere, Finland. It is also known as Metso ('Capercaillie'), due to its resemblance to the bird, when viewed from above.

facts.fact: Reima and Raili Pietilä designed the library in the organic architecture style.
facts.quote: The library was designed by architects Reima and Raili Pietilä in the organic architecture style.

facts.fact: The Pietiläs' entry, Soidinmenot ('Lek mating'), won the 1978 design contest unanimously.
facts.quote: The design contest was held in 1978, with the Pietiläs' proposal Soidinmenot ('Lek mating') winning by unanimous decision.

facts.fact: A visit to Ireland led the architects to draw on Celtic patterns, animal shapes and glacial formations.
facts.quote: Inspired by the architects' visit to Ireland during the initial ideas phase, their design language was influenced by Celtic patterns, animal shapes and glacial formations.

facts.fact: The exterior is made of granite, wiborgite, copper and glass.
facts.quote: The building exterior is made of granite, wiborgite, copper and glass.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1983 and the library opened in August 1986.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1983, and the library opened to the public in August 1986.

facts.fact: The facilities are laid out over three floors.
facts.quote: The facilities are laid out over three floors.

facts.fact: A renovation costing over €11 million was carried out in 2015–2017.
facts.quote: A comprehensive renovation was carried out in 2015-2017, at a cost of over €11 million, to refurbish the facilities and bring them better in line with modern requirements.

facts.fact: A museum and educational centre in Hamarøy, Norway, dedicated to the life and work of the writer Knut Hamsun.
facts.quote: The Knut Hamsun Centre (Norwegian: Hamsunsenteret) is a museum and educational centre in Hamarøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is dedicated to the life and work of the writer Knut Hamsun.

facts.fact: Steven Holl was first contacted about designing the centre in 1994.
facts.quote: The architect Steven Holl was first contacted about designing a centre for Knut Hamsun in 1994.

facts.fact: Holl drew on the local landscape, Norwegian stave churches and sod roofs, and Hamsun's early novels Hunger and Mysteries.
facts.quote: Holl was inspired by the Hamarøy nature and scenery, by Norwegian building tradition with stave churches and sod roofs, and by Hamsun's literature—especially the early works Hunger (1890) and Mysteries (1892).

facts.fact: Holl's concept for the museum was 'Building as a Body: Battleground of invisible Forces', realised inside and out.
facts.quote: Steven Holl has described the Knut Hamsun Centre as "concretizing a Hamsun character in architectonic terms", and he continues: "The concept for the museum, 'Building as a Body:Battleground of invisible Forces,' is realized from inside and out."

facts.fact: Local authorities moved the site from Hamsun's childhood home to Presteid, 5 km east, where he also spent much of his childhood.
facts.quote: Holl originally wanted the centre to be built close to Hamsun's childhood home in Hamsund, but local authorities moved it 5 km east, to Presteid, where Knut Hamsun spent a significant part of his childhood with his uncle.

facts.fact: The building was finished on 4 August 2009, the 150th anniversary of Hamsun's birth.
facts.quote: The Knut Hamsun Centre was finished on August 4, 2009, the 150th anniversary of Knut Hamsun's birth, and the exhibition about Hamsun's life and work opened for the public in June 2010.

facts.fact: The design drew much debate and has won several national and international architecture awards.
facts.quote: The buildings' design has generated considerable attention and debate, and the Knut Hamsun Centre has received several national and international architecture awards.

facts.fact: An early modernist house built by Robert Mallet-Stevens for art patrons Charles and Marie-Laure de Noailles between 1923 and 1927, in the hills above Hyères.
facts.quote: Villa Noailles (French pronunciation: [vi.la no.aj]) is an early modernist house, built by architect Robert Mallet-Stevens for art patrons Charles and Marie-Laure de Noailles, between 1923 and 1927. It is located in the hills above Hyères, in the Var, southeastern France.

facts.fact: Construction took three years and included a triangular Cubist garden by Gabriel Guevrekian.
facts.quote: Construction took three years, and eventually also included a triangular Cubist garden designed by Gabriel Guevrekian.

facts.fact: The villa appears prominently in Man Ray's film Les Mystères du Château de Dé.
facts.quote: Villa Noailles features prominently in Man Ray's film Les Mystères du Château de Dé.

facts.fact: In 1940 the Italian Army occupied the villa and turned it into a hospital.
facts.quote: In 1940 the villa was occupied by the Italian Army and turned into a hospital.

facts.fact: The villa is now an arts centre used for exhibitions.
facts.quote: The villa is now used as an arts center and for special exhibits.

facts.fact: Mallet-Stevens designed his 'Transat' armchair for the villa's swimming pool, among furniture by leading designers of the day.
facts.quote: The decoration included furniture bought or made specially for the villa, by Mallet-Stevens himself with his armchair « Transat » created for the swimming pool, by Djo-Bourgeois, Francis Jourdain, Pierre Legrain, Pierre Chareau, Jean Prouvé, Eileen Gray, Charlotte Perriand, Dominique (Marie André Domin), Sybold van Ravesteyn and Theo van Doesburg from De Stijl, the Wassily Chair of Marcel Breuer, or from the brands Smith & Co and Ronéo, as well as textiles by Raoul Dufy and Sonia Delaunay, luminaires by Jean Perzel, ironworks by Claudius Linossier, stained glass by Louis Barillet and pieces of art : sculptures by Jean and Joël Martel, Henri Laurens, Constantin Brâncuși, Alberto Giacometti, Jacques Lipchitz, paintings by Mondrian or Braque, etc.

facts.fact: The last building designed by Jørn Utzon, planned with his son Kim not as a museum but as a place for architecture students to meet and discuss ideas.
facts.quote: The Utzon Center in Aalborg, Denmark, was the last building to be designed by Jørn Utzon, the architect behind the Sydney Opera House. In collaboration with his son Kim, who provided the final construction drawings, he planned the centre not as a museum but as a place where students of architecture could meet and discuss their ideas for the future.

facts.fact: It stands on the Limfjord waterfront in Utzon's childhood city and was completed in 2008, the year he died.
facts.quote: Located on the Limfjord waterfront in the city where Utzon spent his childhood, the building was completed in 2008, the year Utzon died.

facts.fact: Plans for a 2,700 square metre exhibition and research centre were presented in August 2005, when Utzon was 87.
facts.quote: In August 2005, when he was 87 years old, the plans Utzon and his son Kim had completed for a 2,700 square metre exhibition and research centre on the Aalborg waterfront were presented to the press.

facts.fact: Its reflective, curved roofs enclose tent-like spaces that recall Utzon's time in the Middle East and the Mediterranean.
facts.quote: With its highly reflective, dramatically curved rooftops, the centre cannot be missed. The rather tent-like spaces they enclose are reminiscent of Utzon's times in the Middle East and the Mediterranean.

facts.fact: Separate buildings stand around a courtyard on a platform; tall roofs over the auditorium, boat hall and library rise above the lower exhibition and workshop roofs.
facts.quote: The centre consists of several individual buildings creating a special place around a courtyard on a platform. The tall sculptural roofs of the auditorium and the boathall, both on the harbour front, and the library facing the park area and the city are set off by the lower roofs of the exhibition and workshop areas inside the complex.

facts.fact: Sheltered courtyards inside the complex protect visitors from the wind.
facts.quote: To protect visitors from the wind, Utzon has provided sheltered courtyards inside the complex which also contribute to the pleasure of eating in the outdoor area of the restaurant.

facts.fact: The centre holds an archive of Utzon's original drawings.
facts.quote: There is also an archive of Utzon's original drawings.

facts.fact: The headquarters of Colombia's national archive, in Bogotá, was designed by Rogelio Salmona.
facts.quote: The headquarters are located in the city of Bogotá and was designed by the architect Rogelio Salmona.

facts.fact: The archive holds historical documents dating from 1541 to 1991.
facts.quote: The archive contains historical documents that date from 1541 to 1991.

facts.fact: The Lemke House in Berlin-Alt-Hohenschönhausen was the last house Mies van der Rohe designed in Germany before emigrating to the United States in 1938.
facts.quote: The Lemke House (also Landhaus Lemke or  Mies van der Rohe Haus ) on Oberseestraße 60 in the Berlin district of Alt-Hohenschönhausen is the last house designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe in Germany before his emigration to the United States in 1938.

facts.fact: Work began in summer 1932, after several plans mostly for a two-storey house, and cost 16,000 Reichsmarks.
facts.quote: After several plans, mostly for a two-storey building, work began in the summer of 1932. The costs amounted to 16,000 Reichsmarks (purchasing power adjusted in today's currency: around 61,000 euros).

facts.fact: The L-shaped house is simple and modest, sized for a childless couple.
facts.quote: The L-shaped building is relatively simple and modest, but it also met the requirements of the childless couple.

facts.fact: The façade is red, charcoal-fired brick under a flat roof.
facts.quote: The façade consists of red-coloured, charcoal-fired bricks which, together with the flat roof, make the house look peculiar.

facts.fact: Some furnishings came from Mies's studio or were designed by his partner Lilly Reich.
facts.quote: The furnishings are partly from the studio of Mies van der Rohe or were designed by his partner Lilly Reich.

facts.fact: The Stasi acquired the house in 1962 and changed the house and garden; it was listed as a monument in 1977.
facts.quote: This authority acquired the house in 1962 and made some serious changes to the house and garden. In 1977 the magistrate of Berlin put it on the district monument list.

facts.fact: The house was renovated between 2000 and 2002.
facts.quote: The necessary renovation work followed in the years 2000 to 2002.

facts.fact: Today the house is an exhibition pavilion for modern art.
facts.quote: Today, the house serves as an exhibition pavilion for modern art and attracts the lovers of Mies van der Rohe's architecture.

facts.fact: A museum in Alstahaug, Norway, dedicated to the priest and poet Petter Dass.
facts.quote: The Petter Dass Museum (Norwegian: Petter Dass-museet) in Alstahaug Municipality, Norway is a museum dedicated to the priest and poet Petter Dass.

facts.fact: Work on the new museum building started in September 2005 and it opened on 20 October 2007.
facts.quote: A new museum building and parking facilities were started in September 2005. The opening was postponed several times during 2007, and the museum opened on October 20, 2007.

facts.fact: The new building was designed by Snøhetta.
facts.quote: The building was designed by the Snøhetta architecture office.

facts.fact: It cost about 90 million kroner, paid for by the municipality, county, state and private donors.
facts.quote: The construction of the museum cost about 90 million kr and was funded with support from the municipality, county municipality, and state, as well as private donors.

facts.fact: The courtyard, Alstahaug Church, cemetery and old buildings around it are protected heritage.
facts.quote: The courtyard, Alstahaug Church, cemetery, and buildings are protected by the Norwegian Directorate for Cultural Heritage.

facts.fact: In 1999 Alstahaug was chosen as Nordland county's millennium site, with the museum at its centre.
facts.quote: In 1999, Alstahaug was selected as the millennium site for Nordland county, and the museum played a central role in this.

facts.fact: Spiral, also called the Wacoal Art Center, is a multi-use building in Aoyama, Tokyo, designed by Fumihiko Maki.
facts.quote: Spiral, also known as the Wacoal Art Center, is a multi-use building in Aoyama, Tokyo, Japan, that was designed by architect Fumihiko Maki.

facts.fact: It was commissioned by the lingerie company Wacoal and completed in 1985.
facts.quote: It was commissioned by lingerie company Wacoal and completed in 1985.

facts.fact: It holds exhibition spaces, a multipurpose hall, cafes, restaurants, bars and shops.
facts.quote: Spiral includes exhibition spaces, a multipurpose hall, cafes, restaurants and bars, beauty salons, and select shops.

facts.fact: Its defining feature is a seemingly floating spiral ramp, 15 m across, that circles the rear gallery and climbs to the second floor.
facts.quote: The defining feature of the building is a seemingly-floating spiral ramp (15 m in diameter) that encircles the rear gallery space and climbs to the second floor.

facts.fact: The aluminium and glass façade reflects the jumbled streetscape around it.
facts.quote: The exterior facade of aluminum and glass reflects the jumbled nature of the surrounding streetscape.

facts.fact: It won the AIA's R.S. Reynolds Memorial Award in 1987 and the JIA 25 Years Award in 2012.
facts.quote: The building was selected by the American Institute of Architects for the R.S. Reynolds Memorial Award in 1987. In 2012, the building received the JIA 25 Years Award from the Japan Institute of Architects.

facts.fact: Designed by Hans Poelzig in the New Objectivity style and completed in 1931 as IG Farben's headquarters; it was the Weimar Republic's largest building and Europe's largest office complex until the 1950s.
facts.quote: Designed by Hans Poelzig in the New Objectivity style and completed in 1931, it was built as the corporate headquarters of IG Farben. It was the largest building constructed in the Weimar Republic and remained Europe's largest office complex until the 1950s.

facts.fact: Poelzig won a restricted competition with an elongated, slightly curved main block with six transverse wings and a separate casino building.
facts.quote: The board selected Poelzig's proposal, an elongated, slightly curved main block with six transverse wings and a separate casino building.

facts.fact: The 250-metre main block's six wings join a gently curved corridor, bringing daylight and air to the offices without enclosed courtyards.
facts.quote: The main block is 250 metres long and consists of six wings connected by a gently curved central corridor. The arrangement brought daylight and ventilation to the offices while avoiding the enclosed courtyards common in large office buildings of the period.

facts.fact: A steel frame is faced with travertine, and horizontal window bands stress the curve of the façade.
facts.quote: Its steel frame is faced with travertine, and horizontal window bands emphasise the curve of the façade.

facts.fact: A steel frame, modern cranes and round-the-clock work helped meet a three-year deadline.
facts.quote: A steel frame, modern cranes and round-the-clock working helped meet a three-year deadline, although changes ordered during construction included removing two large end wings and relocating the exhibition hall to create the rear rotunda.

facts.fact: The restored paternoster lifts still run.
facts.quote: The building's restored paternoster lifts remain in operation.

facts.fact: After American forces took Frankfurt in March 1945, the building became a headquarters of the Allied and American military administrations.
facts.quote: After American forces occupied Frankfurt in March 1945, the building became a headquarters for the Allied and American military administrations.

facts.fact: Dissing+Weitling adapted the listed building for Goethe University; it reopened on 26 October 2001.
facts.quote: The Danish practice Dissing+Weitling won the architectural competition to adapt the listed building, balancing university use with the preservation of Poelzig's design. The refurbished building reopened on 26 October 2001 and became the first major element of the Westend Campus.

facts.fact: The original church on the site, built in the 1890s, was badly damaged in a bombing raid in 1943.
facts.quote: The original church on the site was built in the 1890s. It was badly damaged in a bombing raid in 1943.

facts.fact: The present church, foyer, separate belfry and chapel were built between 1959 and 1963, and the damaged spire of the old church was kept as a memorial hall.
facts.quote: The present building, which consists of a church with an attached foyer and a separate belfry with an attached chapel, was built between 1959 and 1963. The damaged spire of the old church has been retained and its ground floor has been made into a memorial hall.

facts.fact: Egon Eiermann won the 1956 competition and first proposed tearing down the old spire; a public outcry made him keep the ruined tower.
facts.quote: The competition's winner, architect Egon Eiermann, initially proposed, in both his submissions, for the remnant of the old spire to be torn down, in favor of a completely new construction but that plan provoked a public outcry in which the ruined tower was characterized as the "heart of Berlin"; as a result Eiermann revised the design to preserve the tower.

facts.fact: The church has an octagonal plan and the tower a hexagonal one, set on a plateau 100 m long and 40 m wide.
facts.quote: The plan of the church is octagonal while the plan of the tower is hexagonal. These components are sited on a plateau measuring 100 metres long and 40 metres wide.

facts.fact: The church walls are a concrete honeycomb holding 21,292 stained glass inlays by Gabriel Loire, inspired by Chartres Cathedral.
facts.quote: The walls of the church are made of a concrete honeycomb containing 21,292 stained glass inlays. The glass, designed by Gabriel Loire, was inspired by the colours of the glass in Chartres Cathedral.

facts.fact: The glass is mostly blue, with small areas of ruby red, emerald green and yellow.
facts.quote: The predominant colour is blue, with small areas of ruby red, emerald green and yellow.

facts.fact: The church is 35 m across and 20.5 m high and seats over 1,000.
facts.quote: The church is 35 metres in diameter and 20.5 metres high with a capacity of over 1,000.

facts.fact: The church is a famous landmark of western Berlin, nicknamed 'the hollow tooth' by Berliners.
facts.quote: The Memorial Church today is a famous landmark of western Berlin, and is nicknamed by Berliners "der hohle Zahn", meaning "the hollow tooth".

facts.fact: Fariborz Sahba designed it as a half-open lotus of 27 free-standing, marble-clad concrete petals in three rings of nine around a central hall; it was dedicated in December 1986.
facts.quote: Designed by the architect Fariborz Sahba, it takes the form of a half-open lotus of 27 free-standing marble-clad concrete petals, arranged in three rings of nine around a central hall. It was dedicated on 24 December 1986 and opened to the public on 1 January 1987.

facts.fact: Sahba was chosen in 1976 from 45 architects in a worldwide competition.
facts.quote: Fariborz Sahba, one of 45 architects who entered a worldwide competition held for the project, was selected in 1976.

facts.fact: Sahba chose the lotus because several of India's religions, including Hinduism and Buddhism, hold it sacred.
facts.quote: He chose the shape of the lotus because it is considered sacred by several of India's religions, including Hinduism and Buddhism, and symbolizes purity in some traditions.

facts.fact: Like all Baháʼí Houses of Worship it had to be nine-sided and circular; the 27 petals rise in threes from nine arches set in a circle.
facts.quote: The design of the temple follows the requirement set for all Baháʼí Houses of Worship by ʻAbdu'l-Bahá: they had to be nine-sided and circular. Sahba's lotus is built from 27 petals, which rise in threes from nine arches set in a circle.

facts.fact: The thin concrete shells are clad outside in white Pentelic marble from Greece; inside, the white concrete is hand-hammered to a texture.
facts.quote: The petals facing outside of the temple are clad with white Pentelic marble from Greece, while the interior side that faces the hall is white concrete hammered by hand to a textured finish.

facts.fact: It is cooled like a desert wind tower: air passes over the pools, enters the basement, rises through the hall and leaves through vents in the crown.
facts.quote: The temple was designed to be cooled by natural ventilation using the principle of the desert wind tower: outside air passes over the pools, is drawn into the basement, and then rises through the hall and leaves through the vents in the crown.

facts.fact: Nine pools stand for the lotus leaves, so the flower seems to float.
facts.quote: Nine pools surround the building and stand for the leaves of the lotus so that the flower appears to float.

facts.fact: It won awards from the Institution of Structural Engineers and the American Concrete Institute, and India placed it on its World Heritage tentative list in 2014.
facts.quote: Reviewers compared it with the Sydney Opera House on its completion, and it received awards from bodies including the Institution of Structural Engineers and the American Concrete Institute. India placed it on its World Heritage tentative list in 2014.

facts.fact: The arena was built for the 1968 Summer Olympics and opened that year.
facts.quote: The stadium was constructed for the 1968 Summer Olympics and opened in 1968.

facts.fact: It was built specifically for the 1968 Olympic basketball tournament but designed as a multipurpose arena.
facts.quote: The Palacio de los Deportes was constructed specifically for the basketball tournament during the 1968 Summer Olympics.  However, the Palacio was designed to be a multipurpose arena.

facts.fact: The structure was designed by Félix Candela, Enrique Castañeda Tamborel and Antonio Peyri.
facts.quote: The structure was designed by architects Félix Candela, Enrique Castañeda Tamborel and Antonio Peyri.

facts.fact: The circular building has a square-patterned dome spanning 120 m.
facts.quote: The Palacio is circular in design with a square-patterned dome spanning 380 feet (120 m) and enclosing an area of 6.7 acres (27,000 m2).

facts.fact: The dome is made of hyperbolic paraboloids of tubular aluminium, covered in copper-sheathed plywood and carried on huge steel arches.
facts.quote: The dome consists of hyperbolic paraboloids of tubular aluminum covered with waterproof copper-sheathed plywood and supported by huge steel arches.

facts.fact: ICA built it between October 1966 and September 1968, a month before the Games.
facts.quote: It was built by the company ICA between October 15, 1966, and September 13, 1968, and finished construction one month before the Olympics.

facts.fact: It originally seated 22,370, including 7,370 removable seats.
facts.quote: The Palacio originally seated 22,370, including 7,370 in removable seats.

facts.fact: Echoes earned it the nickname 'Palace of Reverberations', and its acoustics were reworked in the 1990s.
facts.quote: The structure underwent a series of modifications during the 1990s to adjust the acoustic profile of the structure.

facts.fact: An art museum in Tokyo's Minato district housing Nezu Kaichirō's private collection of pre-modern Japanese and East Asian art.
facts.quote: The museum is home to the private collection of pre-modern Japanese and East Asian art assembled by Nezu Kaichirō (1860–1940).

facts.fact: After renovation from 2006, the museum reopened in autumn 2009 in a new building designed by Kengo Kuma.
facts.quote: Closed due to large-scale renovation and renewal starting in 2006, the museum reopened in the fall of 2009 with a brand new building designed by the Japanese architect Kengo Kuma.

facts.fact: The museum is also famous for its garden.
facts.quote: The museum is also famous for its garden.

facts.fact: Ogata Kōrin's Irises screen, a National Treasure, is shown each April to May when the irises bloom in the museum's Japanese garden.
facts.quote: This byōbu is displayed for a limited time each year during a special exhibition from April to May to coincide with the blooming season of the irises planted in the museum's Japanese garden.

facts.fact: The collection holds more than 7,400 objects, seven of them National Treasures.
facts.quote: The museum houses more than 7,400 cultural objects, seven of which have been designated by the Japanese government as National Treasures, 88 as Important Cultural Properties, and 94 as Important Art Objects (ja).

facts.fact: Kuma received the 2010 Mainichi Art Award for the Nezu Museum.
facts.quote: 2010 Mainichi Art Award for “Nezu Museum”

facts.fact: Bruno Taut's Wohnstadt Carl Legien is a 1920s social housing project and part of the Berlin Modernism Housing Estates World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: Bruno Taut's "Wohnstadt Carl Legien", a social housing project of the 1920s and part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Berlin Modernism Housing Estates, bears his name as well as several streets all over Germany.

facts.fact: The 11,500-seat Palazzo dello Sport was built for the 1960 Summer Olympics alongside the smaller Palazzetto.
facts.quote: The venue was constructed along with the 11,500-seat Palazzo dello Sport, for the 1960 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: Nervi's Palazzo dello Sport at EUR is now called PalaLottomatica.
facts.quote: Palazzo dello sport EUR (now PalaLottomatica), Rome (1956)

facts.fact: Oslo's municipal building houses the city council and administration; it was built from 1931 to 1950, with a break during the Second World War.
facts.quote: It houses the city council, the city's administration  and various other municipal organisations. The building as it stands today was constructed between 1931 and 1950, with an interruption during the Second World War.

facts.fact: Arnstein Arneberg and Magnus Poulsson won the competition in 1918 with a project clearly inspired by Stockholm City Hall.
facts.quote: In 1918 Arnstein Arneberg and Magnus Poulsson were selected as winners, whose project was clearly inspired by Stockholm City Hall.

facts.fact: Their final 1930 design was reshaped by functionalism, most visibly by adding two office towers.
facts.quote: In 1930 they present their final draft, which had undergone significant changes, influenced by functionalism. The most apparent change was the addition of two office towers.

facts.fact: It is built of red brick with two towers, 63 and 66 metres tall.
facts.quote: Oslo City Hall is built of red brick and has two towers, one 63 meters tall and other 66 meters tall.

facts.fact: Its bricks are larger than usual for the time, roughly the size of medieval bricks.
facts.quote: The bricks used are larger than what was typical at the time of construction, but are roughly the same size as bricks used in the Middle Ages.

facts.fact: The main hall, decorated by Henrik Sørensen and Alf Rolfsen, is 31 m wide, 39 m long and about 21 m high.
facts.quote: The building's main hall was decorated by Henrik Sørensen and Alf Rolfsen. The Hall is 31 metres wide, 39 metres long and around 21 metres high.
