facts.fact: By the time it opened in 1950, its style was no longer popular.
facts.quote: By the time it opened in 1950, the style of the building was no longer popular.

facts.fact: The Nobel Peace Prize ceremony is held there every December.
facts.quote: Various events and ceremonies take place in the building, notably the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony, which takes place every December.

facts.fact: Between 1900 and 1913 Hector Guimard designed the first generation of entrances to the Paris Metro's underground stations.
facts.quote: Between 1900 and 1913, Hector Guimard was responsible for the first generation of entrances to the underground stations of the Paris Metro.

facts.fact: His Art Nouveau designs in cast iron and glass, with his own lettering, created the 'Métro style' and popularised Art Nouveau.
facts.quote: His Art Nouveau designs in cast iron and glass dating mostly to 1900, and the associated lettering that he also designed, created what became known as the Métro style (style Métro) and popularized Art Nouveau.

facts.fact: Guimard used cast iron set in concrete instead of stone, to cut costs and suit the sinuous forms, painted green like weathered brass.
facts.quote: Rather than stone, Guimard used cast iron set in concrete both to reduce costs and to suit the sinuous Art Nouveau forms; they were painted in a green emulating weathered brass.

facts.fact: He designed standardised parts, including railing cartouches with the letter 'M' and signs in his own lettering.
facts.quote: He designed standardized components, including railing cartouches incorporating the letter "M" and signs in his own distinctive lettering reading "Métropolitain" or, at narrow entrances, "Métro"; later the use of the lettering was extended to a holder for a system map and for advertising (porte-plan) with the station name above.

facts.fact: The glass-roofed édicule entrances came to be called libellules because they look like dragonflies.
facts.quote: These édicule types of entrance, which have come to be called libellules because they resemble dragonflies, in some cases had decorated wall panels surfaced in reconstituted lava.

facts.fact: Sign holders rise on sinuous stalks likened to lily of the valley, each with a red-orange globe light.
facts.quote: At many of the entourages, the top of the steps is surmounted by a "Métropolitain" or "Métro" sign in a holder that extends between two risers in the form of sinuous stalks, traditionally compared to lily of the valley (brin de muguet), each bearing a light in the form of a red-orange globe reminiscent of an eye or a flower.

facts.fact: His 1904 design for the Opéra station was rejected and his work for the Metro ended; many entrances were later demolished.
facts.quote: In 1904 his design for the Opéra station at Place de l'Opéra was rejected and his association with the Métro ended; many of his station entrances have been demolished, including all three of the pavilion type (at Bastille and on Avenue de Wagram at Étoile).

facts.fact: Eighty-six entrances survive and are protected as historical monuments, including original glass-roofed édicules at Porte Dauphine and Abbesses.
facts.quote: Eighty-six are still extant and protected as historical monuments; six were protected in 1965, the remainder in 1978. These include two original Type B édicules: at Porte Dauphine, on its original site and with the wall panels, and at Abbesses (moved from Hôtel de Ville in 1974).

facts.fact: The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Sebastian, the patron saint of Rio de Janeiro.
facts.quote: The church is dedicated to Saint Sebastian, the patron saint of Rio de Janeiro.

facts.fact: Edgar de Oliveira da Fonseca designed it in a modern style based on Mayan pyramids.
facts.quote: The cathedral was designed by Edgar de Oliveira da Fonseca in a modern style based on Mayan architectural style of pyramids.

facts.fact: It was built between 1964 and 1979, replacing a series of older churches that had served as cathedral since 1676.
facts.quote: The current cathedral was built between 1964 and 1979 and replaced as seat of the Archdiocese a series of churches that had served as cathedrals since 1676, the most recent and notable of those being the Church of Our Lady of Mount Carmel of the Ancient See, now known as the Old Cathedral, built in the 18th century, and that had been declared Rio's cathedral in the early 19th century.

facts.fact: The conical building is 96 m across inside, 106 m outside and 75 m high.
facts.quote: Conical in form and with a 96 metres (315 ft) internal diameter — 106 metres of external diameter — and an overall height of 75 metres (246 ft).

facts.fact: It has 5,000 seats and standing room for 20,000 people.
facts.quote: Inside, the area measures 8,000 square meters and sufficient 5,000 seats (it has a standing-room capacity of 20,000 people).

facts.fact: Four straight stained glass windows rise 64 m from floor to ceiling.
facts.quote: The cathedral's four rectilinear stained glass windows soar 64 metres (210 ft) from floor to ceiling.

facts.fact: Scotland Street School Museum, in Mackintosh's 1906 school building, opened in 1990.
facts.quote: The growth in public interest has led to refurbishment of long-neglected buildings and increased public access: Scotland Street School Museum housed in Mackintosh's 1906 school building opened in 1990.

facts.fact: A national archaeological museum in Giza, the largest museum in the world devoted to a single civilisation.
facts.quote: Dedicated to Egyptian civilization and its culture, society, and artifacts, the GEM is the largest museum in the world for a single civilization.

facts.fact: The design competition drew 1,557 entries from 82 countries, the second largest architectural competition in history.
facts.quote: The organisers received 1,557 entries from 82 countries, making it the second largest architectural competition in history.

facts.fact: Róisín Heneghan and Shi-Fu Peng won the competition with their firm Heneghan Peng Architects.
facts.quote: The competition was won by architects Róisín Heneghan and Shi-Fu Peng, and their company Heneghan Peng Architects of Ireland; the prize was US$250,000.

facts.fact: The building is a chamfered triangle 2 km northwest of the pyramids, its north and south walls lined up with the pyramids of Khufu and Menkaure.
facts.quote: The building's shape is a chamfered triangle. It sits on a site 2 kilometres (1.2 miles) northwest of the pyramids, near a motorway interchange. The building's north and south walls line up directly with the Great Pyramid of Khufu and the Pyramid of Menkaure.

facts.fact: A plaza of date palms leads to a façade of translucent alabaster stone.
facts.quote: The front of the museum includes a large plaza filled with date palms and a façade made of translucent alabaster stone.

facts.fact: The Grand Staircase, six storeys and about 50 m tall, is a gallery of more than 60 artefacts rising to a terrace with a view of the pyramids.
facts.quote: Spanning 6,000 m2 (65,000 ft2), the structure stands six stories tall (approximately 50 m (160 ft)), connecting the main lobby (atrium), temporary exhibition halls, and the main archaeological storeroom to the upper terrace, offering another view of the Giza Pyramids.

facts.fact: The 10,000 m² atrium has a glass roof and transparent façade through which the pyramids can be seen.
facts.quote: The Atrium (Great Hall) of the Grand Egyptian Museum is the main entrance hall, spanning 10,000 square meters. Designed with a glass roof and a transparent façade, the Giza Pyramids are visible from inside.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2005, the building was completed in 2023 at a cost of $1.2 billion, and it opened officially on 1 November 2025.
facts.quote: The GEM was first announced in 1992, actual construction began in 2005, and it was fully completed in 2023 at a cost of $1.2 billion. Trial opening began in October 2024, and the official opening took place on 1 November 2025.

facts.fact: A linked pair of 88-storey supertall skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur, 451.9 m tall; they were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.
facts.quote: The Petronas Towers (Malay: Menara Berkembar Petronas), also known as the Petronas Twin Towers and colloquially the KLCC Twin Towers, are an interlinked pair of 88-storey supertall skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, standing at 451.9 m (1,483 ft). From 1998 to 2004, they were the tallest buildings in the world until they were surpassed by the Taipei 101 skyscraper in Taiwan.

facts.fact: César Pelli chose a distinctive postmodern style to create a 21st-century icon for Kuala Lumpur.
facts.quote: The towers were designed by Argentine-American architect César Pelli. A distinctive postmodern style was chosen to create a 21st-century icon for Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

facts.fact: The towers are mostly reinforced concrete, with a steel and glass façade designed to recall motifs from Islamic art.
facts.quote: The 88-floor towers are constructed largely of reinforced concrete, with a steel and glass facade designed to resemble motifs found in Islamic art, a reflection of Malaysia's Muslim religion.

facts.fact: The cross section is based on the Rub el Hizb star, with circular sectors added for office space.
facts.quote: Another Islamic influence on the design is that the cross section of the towers is based on a Rub el Hizb, albeit with circular sectors added to meet office space requirements.

facts.fact: Because importing steel was so costly, the towers were built of super high-strength reinforced concrete.
facts.quote: Due to the huge cost of importing steel, the towers were constructed on a cheaper radical design of super high-strength reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: Concrete cores 23 m square and an outer ring of widely spaced super columns give column-free office space.
facts.quote: Supported by 23-by-23-metre (75 ft × 75 ft) concrete cores and an outer ring of widely spaced super columns, the towers use a sophisticated structural system that accommodates its slender profile and provides 560,000 m2 (6,000,000 sq ft) of column-free office space.

facts.fact: The skybridge between the towers is 170 m above the ground and 58.4 m long.
facts.quote: The bridge is 170 m (558 ft) above the ground and 58.4 m (192 ft) long, weighing 750 t (830 tons).

facts.fact: A double-decker skybridge links the towers on the 41st and 42nd floors.
facts.quote: The towers feature a double decker skybridge connecting the two towers on the 41st and 42nd floors, holding the record for the highest 2-story bridge in the world.

facts.fact: Pelli received the Aga Khan Award for Architecture for the design of the towers.
facts.quote: That year, Pelli received the Aga Khan Award for Architecture for the design of the Petronas Towers  Pelli's design for the National Museum of Art in Osaka, Japan, was completed 2005, the same year that Pelli's firm changed its name to Pelli Clarke Pelli Architects to reflect the growing roles of senior principals Fred W. Clarke and Pelli's son Rafael.

facts.fact: It was the world's tallest building from its opening on 31 December 2004 until the Burj Khalifa surpassed it.
facts.quote: It was officially classified as the world's tallest building from its opening on 31 December 2004 until it was surpassed by the Burj Khalifa in 2009.

facts.fact: C. Y. Lee directed its design.
facts.quote: He directed the design of Taipei 101, the world's tallest skyscraper at the time of completion, in 2004.

facts.fact: Its postmodernist and neo-futurist style evokes traditional Asian aesthetics in a modern structure of industrial materials.
facts.quote: Taipei 101's postmodernist and neo-futurist architectural style evokes traditional Asian aesthetics in a modern structure employing industrial materials.

facts.fact: The tower is a series of eight segments of eight floors each; eight is linked with prosperity and good fortune in Chinese-speaking cultures.
facts.quote: The main tower features a series of eight segments of eight floors each. In Chinese-speaking cultures the number eight is associated with abundance, prosperity and good fortune.

facts.fact: The repeated segments recall a pagoda, a bamboo stalk and a stack of ancient Chinese money boxes.
facts.quote: The repeated segments simultaneously recall the rhythms of an Asian pagoda (a tower linking earth and sky, also evoked in the Petronas Towers), a stalk of bamboo (an icon of learning and growth), and a stack of ancient Chinese ingots or money boxes (a symbol of abundance).

facts.fact: Being only 200 m from a major fault line, it uses outrigger trusses every eight floors to tie the core columns to the outer ones.
facts.quote: Because of the height of Taipei 101, combined with the surrounding area's geology—the building is located just 660 ft (200 m) away from a major fault line—outrigger trusses, located at eight-floor intervals, connect the columns in the building's core to those on the exterior.

facts.fact: A 660-tonne steel pendulum, hung from the 92nd to the 88th floor, acts as a tuned mass damper against strong gusts.
facts.quote: Motioneering designed a 660-metric-ton (728-short-ton) steel pendulum that serves as a tuned mass damper, at a cost of NT$132 million (US$4 million). Suspended from the 92nd to the 88th floor, the pendulum sways to offset movements in the building caused by strong gusts.

facts.fact: A wind-tunnel study led to the 'double stairstep' corners, which sharply reduce crosswind oscillation.
facts.quote: A double chamfered step design was found to dramatically reduce this crosswind oscillation, resulting in the final design's "double stairstep" corner facade.

facts.fact: In 2011 it received LEED Platinum certification, becoming the tallest and largest green building in the world.
facts.quote: In 2011, Taipei 101 was awarded a Platinum certificate rating under the LEED certification system for energy efficiency and environmental design, becoming the tallest and largest green building in the world.

facts.fact: A 540.1 m television and radio tower in Moscow designed by Nikolai Nikitin; it is the tallest free-standing structure in Europe.
facts.quote: Standing 540.1 metres (1,772 ft), it was designed by Nikolai Nikitin. As of 2026, it is the tallest free-standing structure in Europe and 15th tallest in the world.

facts.fact: It was the first free-standing structure to exceed 500 m, and was built to mark the 50th anniversary of the October Revolution.
facts.quote: The tower was the first free-standing structure to exceed 500 m (1,600 ft) in height. Ostankino was built to mark the 50th anniversary of the October Revolution.

facts.fact: Nikitin proposed reinforced concrete instead of the competition-winning steel lattice, citing a tower completed in Stuttgart in 1956.
facts.quote: He suggested building the tower out of reinforced concrete, citing a successful similar project in Stuttgart that had been completed two years prior, in 1956.

facts.fact: Nikitin used taut steel ropes to keep the concrete frame strong and stable.
facts.quote: To ensure the strength and stability of the concrete frame, Nikitin incorporated 149 taut steel ropes.

facts.fact: Nikitin's 540 m design had a very small foundation, with only a 4.6 m base underground.
facts.quote: Nikolai Nikitin suggested constructing a 540 metres (1,770 ft) rocket, but the proposed tower had minimal foundation, with only a 4.6-meter base underground.

facts.fact: Arches between the supports and porthole windows in the upper cone give the tower a striking likeness to a rocket.
facts.quote: They incorporated arches between the supports, constructed a glazed cylinder beneath the tower trunk to accommodate technical services and live broadcasting studios, and integrated illuminator windows in the upper section of the cone, giving the tower a striking similarity to a rocket.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1959, with a whole town built for the project.
facts.quote: The construction work commenced in 1959, leading to the establishment of an entire town dedicated to the project.

facts.fact: A fire on 27 August 2000 damaged the structure; only 19 of its 150 steel cables survived intact.
facts.quote: On 27 August 2000, a devastating blaze not only engulfed the Seventh Heaven restaurant but also caused extensive damage to the entire structure. Out of the 150 steel cables that once held the building together, only 19 remained intact after the fire had subsided.

facts.fact: The national mosque of Pakistan, in Islamabad.
facts.quote: The Faisal Mosque is the national mosque of Pakistan, located in Islamabad, the capital of the country.

facts.fact: Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay's design won a 1969 international competition with 43 proposals from 17 countries.
facts.quote: In 1969, an international competition was held in which architects from 17 countries submitted 43 proposals. The winning design was that of Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay.

facts.fact: Instead of a dome, the mosque is shaped like a Bedouin tent, ringed by four 90 m minarets.
facts.quote: Without a typical dome, the mosque is shaped like a Bedouin tent, surrounded by four 90 m (300 ft)-tall minarets.

facts.fact: Eight-sided sloping shell roofs form a triangular prayer hall for 10,000 worshippers.
facts.quote: The design features eight-sided shell shaped sloping roofs forming a triangular worship hall which can hold 10,000 worshippers.

facts.fact: The main prayer hall is carried by four concrete girders, and the minarets are inspired by Turkish architecture.
facts.quote: The main structure of the building is the main prayer hall, which is supported by four concrete girders. The four unusual minarets are inspired by Turkish architecture.

facts.fact: The interior is white marble with mosaics and calligraphy by the Pakistani artist Sadequain and a Turkish-style chandelier.
facts.quote: The interior of the main tent-shaped hall is covered in white marble and decorated with mosaics and calligraphy by the famous Pakistani artist Sadequain, and a Turkish-style chandelier.

facts.fact: It stands at the foot of the Margalla Hills, at the north end of Faisal Avenue.
facts.quote: It is situated at the north end of Faisal Avenue, putting it at the northernmost end of the city and at the foot of Margalla Hills, the westernmost foothills of the Himalayas.

facts.fact: It was the largest mosque in the world from 1986 to 1993.
facts.quote: Faisal Mosque was the largest mosque in the world from 1986 until 1993 when it was overtaken by the mosques in Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: A modified version of Dalokay's unbuilt design for Ankara's Kocatepe Mosque became the basis for the Faisal Mosque.
facts.quote: Later, a modified design was used as a basis for the Faisal Mosque in Islamabad, Pakistan.

facts.fact: A mixed-use supertall skyscraper in Pudong, Shanghai, designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox for the Mori Building Company.
facts.quote: The Shanghai World Financial Center (SWFC; Chinese: 上海环球金融中心; pinyin: Shànghǎi Huánqiú Jīnróng Zhōngxīn, Shanghainese: Zånhae Guejieu Cinyon Tsonsin) is a supertall skyscraper located in the Pudong district of Shanghai. It was designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and developed by the Mori Building Company, with Leslie E. Robertson Associates as its structural engineer and China State Construction Engineering Corporation and Shanghai Construction (Group) General Co. as its main contractor.

facts.fact: It holds offices, hotels, conference rooms and a ground-floor shopping mall.
facts.quote: It is a mixed-use skyscraper, consisting of offices, hotels, conference rooms, and a ground-floor shopping mall.

facts.fact: Topped out at 492 m in 2007, it was the world's second-tallest building on completion and the tallest by roof height.
facts.quote: On 14 September 2007, the skyscraper was topped out at 492 meters (1,614.2 ft), making it the 2nd tallest building in the world on completion (the tallest at the time being Taipei 101), the tallest building in the world by roof height only, and the tallest in mainland China.

facts.fact: The trapezoid opening at the top is its most distinctive feature; a circular opening was first planned to reduce wind pressure.
facts.quote: The most distinctive feature of the SWFC's design is the trapezoid aperture at the peak. The original design specified a circular aperture, 46 m (151 ft) in diameter, to reduce the stresses of wind pressure and to reference the Chinese mythological depiction of the sky as a circle.

facts.fact: On 18 October 2005 KPF submitted a new design in which a trapezoidal hole replaced the circle at the top of the tower.
facts.quote: On 18 October 2005, KPF submitted an alternative design to Mori Building and a trapezoidal hole replaced the circle at the top of the tower, which in addition to changing the controversial design, would also be cheaper and easier to implement, according to the architects.

facts.fact: People call it 'the bottle opener'.
facts.quote: Foreigners and Chinese alike informally refer to the building as "the bottle opener".

facts.fact: A diagonal-braced frame with outrigger trusses carries wind and other loads to the ground, saving material in the core walls and perimeter steel.
facts.quote: These compressive and bending forces are carried down to the ground by the diagonal-braced frame (with added outrigger trusses). The design employs an effective use of material, because it decreases the thickness of the outer core shear walls and the weight of the structural steel in the perimeter.

facts.fact: CTBUH named it the best tall building completed in 2008.
facts.quote: Shanghai World Financial Center was named by architects as the best skyscraper completed in 2008, receiving both the Best Tall Building Overall and Asia & Australasia awards from the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH).

facts.fact: A 128-storey, 632 m megatall skyscraper in Lujiazui, Pudong, and the tallest building in China.
facts.quote: The Shanghai Tower is a 128-story, 632-meter-tall (2,073-foot) megatall skyscraper located in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai. It is currently the tallest building in China, the world's third-tallest building by height to architectural top, and the world's second-tallest building by height to highest occupied floor.

facts.fact: Gensler designed it, with Shanghainese architect Jun Xia leading the design team.
facts.quote: The Shanghai Tower was designed by the American architectural firm Gensler, with Shanghainese architect Jun Xia leading the design team.

facts.fact: It is nine cylindrical buildings stacked on top of each other, wrapped by an inner glass façade; between that and the twisting outer layer are nine public zones.
facts.quote: The tower takes the form of nine cylindrical buildings stacked atop each other that total 128 floors, all enclosed by the inner layer of the glass facade. Between that and the outer layer, which twists as it rises, nine indoor zones provide public space for visitors.

facts.fact: Each of the nine zones has its own atrium with gardens, cafés, restaurants and shops.
facts.quote: Each of these nine areas has its own atrium, featuring gardens, cafés, restaurants and retail space, and providing panoramic views of the city.

facts.fact: The glass façade twists 120° as it rises, cutting wind loads by 24% and using 25% less structural steel than a conventional design.
facts.quote: The design of the tower's glass façade, which completes a 120° twist as it rises, is intended to reduce wind loads on the building by 24%. This reduced the amount of construction materials needed; the Shanghai Tower used 25% less structural steel than a conventional design of a similar height.

facts.fact: The double-layered insulating glass façade reduces the need for air conditioning, and heating and cooling use geothermal sources.
facts.quote: The double-layered insulating glass façade was designed to reduce the need for indoor air conditioning, and is composed of an advanced reinforced glass with a high tolerance for temperature variations. In addition, the building's heating and cooling systems use geothermal energy sources.

facts.fact: Construction began on 29 November 2008 and the tower topped out in August 2013.
facts.quote: Groundbreaking and construction work on the tower began on 29 November 2008 and topped out on 4 August 2013.

facts.fact: With the Jin Mao Tower and the Shanghai World Financial Center it forms the world's first group of three adjacent supertall buildings.
facts.quote: The Shanghai Tower joins the Jin Mao Tower and SWFC to form the world's first adjacent grouping of three supertall buildings.

facts.fact: TSE unveiled its new building, designed by Grafton Architects, in 2020.
facts.quote: In 2020, TSE unveiled its new building designed by Grafton Architects, and in the following year, it continued to expand its research focus with the launch of the TSE Health Center, TSE Infrastructure & Network Center, and TSE Competition Policy & Regulation Center.

facts.fact: Kosovo's highest library institution, in Pristina, which collects and preserves the country's documentary and intellectual heritage.
facts.quote: The mission of the library is to collect, preserve, promote and make accessible the documentary and intellectual heritage of Kosovo.

facts.fact: The building was inaugurated on 25 November 1982 and designed by the Croatian architect Andrija Mutnjaković.
facts.quote: The current building of the National Library of Kosovo was inaugurated on 25 November 1982. It was designed by the Croatian architect Andrija Mutnjaković.

facts.fact: Its 16,500 m² have zenith windows under 99 domes of different sizes, and the whole building is wrapped in a metal net.
facts.quote: Its space consists of 16,500 square meters. It is made with zenith windows, with a total 99 domes of different sizes and is entirely covered in a metal fishing net, which have their own particular architectural symbolism.

facts.fact: The largest dome crowns the lobby's high ceiling and brings in plenty of daylight; the lobby floor is a marble mosaic.
facts.quote: The floor of the hall is a unique work of diverse mosaic marble stone. The largest dome of the library is the main ornament of the hall's high ceiling, thus providing ample natural lighting.

facts.fact: The architect said the building blends Byzantine and Islamic architectural forms.
facts.quote: According to the architect of the National Library of Kosovo the building is meant to represent a style blending Byzantine and Islamic architectural forms.

facts.fact: Others see it as a reaction to the impersonal International Style, combining modern means with regional and rural traditions.
facts.quote: By others this building is seen as a reaction to the impersonality of International Style and an attempt to combine modern means with regional traditions and rural architecture, but also as a Modern-Metabolist style.

facts.fact: It has two reading rooms of 300 and 100 seats, a 150-seat amphitheatre and space for about two million volumes.
facts.quote: It houses two reading rooms with 300 and 100 seats respectively, a reading room for periodicals, rooms for special collections, cataloguing and research, a 150-seat amphitheatre and a 75-seat meeting hall. It has the capacity to accommodate about two million volumes.

facts.fact: Its looks are disputed: VirtualTourist ranked it among the ten ugliest buildings in the world.
facts.quote: It was ranked in the top ten ugliest buildings in the world by  VirtualTourist.

facts.fact: An art museum built for Graz's year as European Capital of Culture in 2003; it shows contemporary art from the 1960s on.
facts.quote: The Kunsthaus Graz, Grazer Kunsthaus, or Graz Art Museum was built as part of the European Capital of Culture celebrations in 2003 and has since become an architectural landmark in Graz, Austria. Its exhibition program specializes in contemporary art from the 1960s onwards.

facts.fact: Designed by Colin Fournier and Peter Cook.
facts.quote: Kunsthaus Graz was designed by Colin Fournier and Sir Peter Cook.

facts.fact: An example of blob architecture, its skin of iridescent blue acrylic panels also works as photovoltaic panels.
facts.quote: The building is an example of blob architecture and has a skin made from iridescent blue acrylic panels, which also double as photovoltaic panels.

facts.fact: Its shape and its contrast with its surroundings earned it the name 'Friendly Alien'.
facts.quote: Owing to its shape and its contrast to its surroundings, it is known as the "Friendly Alien".

facts.fact: It incorporates the façade of the Iron House, an iron-framed building of 1848.
facts.quote: The building incorporates the façade of the Iron House, an iron-framed structure built in 1848.

facts.fact: The BIX façade, by realities:united, puts 930 individually dimmable fluorescent lamps inside the acrylic skin on the east side.
facts.quote: The BIX was created inside the acrylic glass skin of the eastern side of the building and it consists of 930 fluorescent lamps, whose brightness can be adjusted individually.

facts.fact: The façade can show films and animations as a large screen.
facts.quote: The façade can be used as a large screen for films and animations in what is referred to as a "communicative display skin".

facts.fact: It was a Stirling Prize finalist in 2004.
facts.quote: 2004 – Finalist for Stirling Prize for Kunsthaus Graz (with Colin Fournier)

facts.fact: The national art museum of Australia, holding more than 166,000 works of art.
facts.quote: The National Gallery of Australia (NGA), formerly the Australian National Gallery, is the national art museum of Australia and one of the largest art museums in Australia, holding more than 166,000 works of art.

facts.fact: Colin Madigan of Edwards Madigan Torzillo and Partners won the design competition in 1968.
facts.quote: In 1968, Colin Madigan of Edwards Madigan Torzillo and Partners won the competition for the design, even though no design could be finalised, as the final site was now in doubt.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1973 and Queen Elizabeth II opened the building in 1982.
facts.quote: The construction of the building commenced in 1973, with the unveiling of a plaque by Prime Minister Gough Whitlam. Construction was managed by P.D.C. Constructions under the supervision of the National Capital Development Commission and it was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1982, during the premiership of Whitlam's successor, Malcolm Fraser.

facts.fact: The building is late 20th-century Brutalist, with angular masses and raw concrete, surrounded by sculpture gardens of Australian native plants.
facts.quote: The National Gallery building is in the late 20th-century Brutalist style.  It is characterised by angular masses and raw concrete surfaces and is surrounded by a series of sculpture gardens planted with Australian native plants and trees.

facts.fact: Its geometry is based on a triangle, seen most clearly in the coffered ceiling grids and floor tiles of the main floor.
facts.quote: The geometry of the building is based on a triangle, most obviously manifested for visitors in the coffered ceiling grids and tiles of the principal floor.

facts.fact: It is mainly built of reinforced bush-hammered concrete, which was originally also the interior wall surface.
facts.quote: The building is principally constructed of reinforced bush hammered concrete, which was also originally the interior wall surface.

facts.fact: The High Court and National Gallery Precinct was added to the Australian National Heritage List in November 2007.
facts.quote: The High Court and National Gallery Precinct were added to the Australian National Heritage List in November 2007.

facts.fact: A new entrance and Indigenous art galleries opened in 2010.
facts.quote: Stage 1 of the Indigenous galleries and new entrance project was officially opened on 30 September 2010 by Quentin Bryce, Governor-General of Australia.

facts.fact: A large conference centre at Takaragaike in Kyoto, where the Kyoto Protocol was signed.
facts.quote: The Kyoto International Conference Center (国立京都国際会館, Kokuritsu Kyōto Kokusai Kaikan), abbreviated as ICC Kyoto and previously called the Kyoto International Conference Hall, is a large conference facility located at Takaragaike, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. The Kyoto Protocol was signed in this hall.

facts.fact: Sachio Otani designed it on an unusual hexagonal framework with few vertical walls or columns; it opened in 1966 with an addition in 1973.
facts.quote: The center was designed by architect Sachio Otani to an unusual hexagonal framework, resulting in few vertical walls or columns, and opened in 1966 with an addition in 1973.

facts.fact: It is a rare surviving example of Metabolism in Japan.
facts.quote: It is a rare remaining example of Metabolism in Japan (the newer and more famous Nakagin Capsule Tower Building was demolished in 2022).

facts.fact: The main Conference Hall has a large meeting room for 2,000 people, with an Annex Hall for 1,500.
facts.quote: Today the total facility provides 156,000 m² of meeting space, and consists of the main Conference Hall with large meeting room (capacity 2,000) and a number of smaller rooms, an Annex Hall (capacity 1,500) and Event Hall, with The Prince Kyoto Takaragaike Hotel nearby.

facts.fact: It hosted the 1997 UN climate change conference that produced the Kyoto Protocol.
facts.quote: 1997 United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (Kyoto Protocol)

facts.fact: Otani began in Kenzo Tange's studio, helping design the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum, before founding his own practice in 1960.
facts.quote: He began his career in Kenzo Tange's studio, where he helped design the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum (1955). In 1960 he started his own practice, and has subsequently designed a number of memorable buildings including the Tokyo Children's Cultural Center (1964), Kyoto International Conference Center (1966), the Kanazawa Institute of Technology (1969), and the Kawaramachi housing project in Kawasaki, Kanagawa (1970).

facts.fact: A 20th-century Catholic Marian shrine church in Syracuse, Sicily, that dominates the skyline on the approach to Ortigia.
facts.quote: The Basilica of the Madonna delle Lacrime (Sanctuary of the Virgin of Tears), also called Madonnina delle Lacrime is a 20th-century Roman Catholic Marian shrine church in Syracuse in Sicily, Italy. The modern building, derided by some as an inverted ice-cream cone, dominates the skyline of the approach to Ortigia.

facts.fact: Michel Andrault and Pierre Parat won the international design competition; Riccardo Morandi was the main engineer.
facts.quote: An international competition was held to design the church, and the design by Michel Andrault and Pierre Parat was selected. The main engineer for construction was Riccardo Morandi.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1966 and was only completed in 1994.
facts.quote: Construction of the shrine began in 1966, but was only complete by 1994.

facts.fact: Building work uncovered a crypt, probably an early Christian mausoleum, now in the church's lower rooms.
facts.quote: During construction, the foundations were found to contain a crypt, likely a paleo-christian mausoleum, now in the inferior rooms of the church.

facts.fact: It is 103 m high, about 30 m shorter than first planned.
facts.quote: The building initially was planned to be larger, but at 103 metres high, it was truncated some 30 metres.

facts.fact: One reading of the design is a giant teardrop striking the earth.
facts.quote: There are various interpretations of the design, including that it is meant to suggest a giant teardrop impacting the earth.

facts.fact: It honours a reported miracle of 1953, when a plaster icon of the Madonna was said to have shed tears.
facts.quote: Others objected to the construction of such a pretentious structure to honour the putative miracle, occurring from August 29 to September 1, 1953, when a plaster icon of the Madonna of the Immaculate Heart was claimed to have shed tears for an indigent local couple, including a fisherman husband.

facts.fact: Pope John Paul II made it a minor basilica in 2002.
facts.quote: In 2002 Pope John Paul II elevated the sanctuary to the status of a minor basilica.

facts.fact: The complex links the city centre with the higher Kanaker-Zeytun district and is a key part of the planning axis of Alexander Tamanyan's master plan for Yerevan.
facts.quote: The complex connects the city center with the elevated areas of the Kanaker-Zeytun administrative district and is an important element of the urban planning axis established in the master plan of Yerevan by architect Alexander Tamanyan.

facts.fact: An architectural and monumental complex of stairs, terraces, fountains, sculptures and exhibition halls in Yerevan.
facts.quote: The Cascade (Armenian: Կասկադ) is an architectural and monumental complex in Yerevan, Armenia, that consists of a multi-level staircase structure with terraces, fountains, sculptures, and exhibition halls.

facts.fact: The idea first appeared in Alexander Tamanian's 1920s master plan, which imagined terraces, waterfalls and flower beds climbing to the northern hills.
facts.quote: The idea for the Cascade first appeared in the master plan for Yerevan, developed by architect Alexander Tamanian in the 1920s. He envisioned connecting the city center with the northern hills of Kanaker through a system of terraces, waterfalls, and flower beds.

facts.fact: In the early 1970s Jim Torosyan, Sargis Gurzadyan and Aslan Mkhitaryan began a new design.
facts.quote: In the early 1970s, architects Jim Torosyan, Sargis Gurzadyan, and Aslan Mkhitaryan began developing a new design for the Cascade.

facts.fact: Torosyan added exhibition halls within the terraces, hidden escalators, courtyards and an open-air sculpture garden.
facts.quote: He added exhibition halls within the terraces, escalators hidden within the complex, courtyards creating cozy relaxation areas, and a sculpture garden—a space for contemporary art in the open air.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1980 but stopped in the late 1980s after the 1988 earthquake and the end of the Soviet Union.
facts.quote: Construction of the cascade began in 1980. However, in the late 1980s, following the 1988 Armenian earthquake, the dissolution of the Soviet Union, and the First Nagorno-Karabakh War, construction was suspended.

facts.fact: Five main terraces are linked by stairs and internal escalators over about 302 m.
facts.quote: The complex consists of five main terraces connected by flights of stairs and internal escalators. The total length of the complex is approximately 302 meters, with 555-572 steps(depends on the sides).

facts.fact: It is built of milky white tuff and travertine.
facts.quote: The construction materials are milky white tuff and travertine.

facts.fact: Gerard Cafesjian's foundation led the restoration from 2002; the Cafesjian Museum of Art, designed with David Hotson, opened in 2009.
facts.quote: The project was initiated by the Gerard Cafesjian Museum Foundation, a museum founded by Armenian-American philanthropist Gerard Cafesjian, who teamed with architect David Hotson to design the museum, which opened in 2009 and became the Cafesjian Museum of Art.

facts.fact: A wing of the Israel Museum in Jerusalem that houses the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Aleppo Codex.
facts.quote: The Shrine of the Book (Hebrew: היכל הספר, Heikhal HaSefer) is a wing of the Israel Museum in the Givat Ram neighborhood of Jerusalem that houses the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Aleppo Codex, among other texts.

facts.fact: It was designed by Armand Bartos, Frederick Kiesler and Gezer Heller over seven years.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Armand Phillip Bartos, Frederick John Kiesler and Gezer Heller over a period of seven years.

facts.fact: A white dome covers a structure set two-thirds below ground, reflected in a surrounding pool.
facts.quote: The shrine is built as a white dome, covering a structure placed two-thirds below the ground, that is reflected in a pool of water that surrounds it.

facts.fact: A black basalt wall faces the white dome.
facts.quote: Across from the white dome is a black basalt wall.

facts.fact: In one reading, the white dome stands for the Sons of Light and the black wall for the Sons of Darkness, from one of the scrolls.
facts.quote: According to one interpretation, the colors and shapes of the building are based on the imagery of the Scroll of the War of the Sons of Light Against the Sons of Darkness; the white dome symbolizes the Sons of Light and the black wall symbolizes the Sons of Darkness.

facts.fact: Because the scrolls are fragile, they are shown in rotation, each resting in storage after 3–6 months on display.
facts.quote: After a scroll has been exhibited for 3–6 months, it is removed from its showcase and placed temporarily in a special storeroom, where it "rests" from exposure.

facts.fact: Some Israeli architects objected to Kiesler and Bartos as architects because they were not Israelis.
facts.quote: Israeli architects disapproved of his and Bartos's serving as the architects for the Shrine of the Book (1957–65) because they were not Israelis, even though they were Jews.

facts.fact: A 14-hectare public park on the left bank of the Seine in Paris's 15th arrondissement.
facts.quote: Parc André-Citroën is a 14 hectares (35 acres) public park located on the left bank of the river Seine in the 15th arrondissement of Paris.

facts.fact: It was built on the site of a former Citroën car factory and, on opening in 1992, was the largest new park in Paris in more than a century.
facts.quote: Built on the site of a former Citroën automobile manufacturing plant, the park is named after company founder André Citroën.  When it opened in 1992, it was the largest park to open in Paris in more than a century.

facts.fact: It was designed from the early 1990s by landscape designers Gilles Clément and Alain Provost with architects Patrick Berger, Jean-François Jodry and Jean-Paul Viguier.
facts.quote: The park was designed beginning of the 1990s by the French landscape designers Gilles Clément and Alain Provost and the architects Patrick Berger, Jean-François Jodry and Jean-Paul Viguier.

facts.fact: It is built around a central rectangular lawn about 273 by 85 m.
facts.quote: The park is built around a central, rectangular lawn of roughly 273 by 85 metres (895' x 279') in size.

facts.fact: Two greenhouse pavilions at the eastern end are separated by a paved area of dancing fountains.
facts.quote: It is embellished with two greenhouse pavilions (hosting exotic plants and Mediterranean vegetation) at the eastern, urban end which are separated by a paved area featuring dancing fountains.

facts.fact: On the north side are six 'Serial Gardens' and a 'Garden in Movement' of wild grasses that respond to the wind.
facts.quote: On the north side are two sets of small gardens: the six "Serial Gardens", each with a distinct landscape and architectural design and a "Garden in Movement" that presents wild grasses selected to respond at different rates to wind velocity.

facts.fact: Each serial garden is linked to a metal, a planet, a day of the week, a state of water and a sense.
facts.quote: The six serial gardens are each associated with a metal, a planet, a day of the week, a state of the water and a sense:

facts.fact: A 630 m diagonal path cuts through the park.
facts.quote: A 630-meter (690 yard) diagonal path cuts through the park.

facts.fact: The Hyvinkää Church of 1961 is one of Aarno Ruusuvuori's best-known works.
facts.quote: His best-known works are the Tapiola Church and the Weilin & Göös Print Works in Espoo (1964–66) and the Hyvinkää Church (1961).

facts.fact: Known as the 'Chapel of Silence', it is a place to calm down and be silent in one of Helsinki's busiest areas.
facts.quote: It is also known as the "Chapel of Silence" since it is intended to be a place to calm down and have a moment of silence in one of the busiest areas of the city.

facts.fact: The chapel is ecumenical and welcomes everyone, whatever their religion or background.
facts.quote: The chapel is ecumenical and welcomes everyone irrespective of religion, philosophy of life or background.

facts.fact: Its interior and exterior are very austere and simple, close to a multi-faith prayer room.
facts.quote: The chapel's overall design (both on the interior and exterior) is very austere and simplistic, as well as mostly neutral, bearing some semblance to a multi-faith prayer room.

facts.fact: No regular church services are held there.
facts.quote: Regular church services are not being held in the chapel, though it is planned to hold regular moments of prayer in the future.

facts.fact: It was built for Helsinki's World Design Capital year in 2012, designed by Kimmo Lintula, Niko Sirola and Mikko Summanen of K2S Architects.
facts.quote: The chapel was constructed as a part of the World Design Capital program in 2012. It was designed by architects Kimmo Lintula, Niko Sirola and Mikko Summanen of K2S Architects Ltd., and won the International Architecture Awards in 2010.

facts.fact: About 250,000 people had visited by January 2013, and 500,000 a year later.
facts.quote: The chapel became popular immediately after it was opened; some 250,000 people had visited by January 2013. A year later, the chapel received its 500,000th visitor.

facts.fact: CNN called it an architectural landmark.
facts.quote: CNN called the building an architectural landmark and said: "The chapel demonstrates how contemporary architecture at its best can fascinate and inspire."

facts.fact: The official residence of the President of India, formerly the Viceroy's House, on Raisina Hill in New Delhi.
facts.quote: The Rashtrapati Bhavan (, ISO: Rāṣṭrapati Bhavana; lit. 'President's House'), formerly Viceroy's House (1931–1947) and Government House (1947–1950) is the official residence of the President of India, located at the western end of Rajpath, Raisina Hill in New Delhi.

facts.fact: Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker designed it, in the Delhi Order based on Indo-Saracenic architecture; it was built from 1912 to 1929.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker in Delhi Order based on Indo-Saracenic architecture. The construction began in 1912 and the building was completed in 1929.

facts.fact: Lutyens's design is grandly classical overall, with colours and details inspired by Indo-Saracenic architecture.
facts.quote: Lutyens' design is grandly classical overall, with colours and details inspired by Indo-Saracenic architecture.

facts.fact: A traditional chhajja replaces the classical frieze, projecting 2.4 m to cast deep shadows and shield the windows from sun and monsoon rain.
facts.quote: There was also a traditional Indian chujja or chhajja, which occupied the place of a frieze in classical architecture; it was a sharp, thin, protruding element which extended 8 feet (2.4 m) from the building, and created deep shadows. It blocks harsh sunlight from the windows and also shields the windows from heavy rain during the monsoon season.

facts.fact: Lutyens invented the 'Delhi Order' for the front columns, fusing acanthus leaves with hanging Indian bells.
facts.quote: The front of the palace, on the east side, has twelve unevenly spaced massive columns with the Delhi Order capitals, a "nonce order" Lutyens invented for this building, with Ashokan details.  The capitals have a fusion of acanthus leaves with the four pendant Indian bells.

facts.fact: Lutyens also drew on early Buddhist Mauryan art: the drum of the main dome recalls the railings of stupas such as Sanchi.
facts.quote: This can be seen in the Dehli Order, and in the main dome, where the drum below has decoration recalling the railings around early Buddhist stupas such as Sanchi.

facts.fact: Its four floors and 340 rooms were built from 700 million bricks and a great deal of stone, with little steel.
facts.quote: Consisting of four floors and 340 rooms, with a floor area of 200,000 square metres (2,200,000 sq ft), it was built using 700 million bricks and 3,000,000 cu ft (85,000 m3) of stone with little steel.

facts.fact: With 200,000 m² of floor area in its H-shaped main building, it is the largest official residence of any head of state.
facts.quote: With over 200,000 square metres (2,200,000 sq ft) of total usable floor area of the H-shaped main building, the Rashtrapati Bhavan is the largest official residence by total floor area of any head of state in the world, followed by, the Istana Nurul Iman in Brunei and the Quirinal Palace in Italy.

facts.fact: The Persian poet and polymath Omar Khayyam, who died in Nishapur in 1131, is buried in what is now the Mausoleum of Omar Khayyam.
facts.quote: Omar Khayyam died at the age of 83 in his hometown of Nishapur on 4 December 1131, and he is buried in what is now the Mausoleum of Omar Khayyam.

facts.fact: Hooshang Seyhoun, who also designed monuments to other Iranian poets and scholars, designed the Tomb of Omar Khayyam.
facts.quote: Seyhoun's architectural innovations also extended to designing monuments honoring Iranian poets and polymaths, such as the acclaimed Tomb of Omar Khayyam.

facts.fact: A 71-storey, 309.6 m office skyscraper in Tianhe, Guangzhou, designed by SOM with Adrian Smith and Gordon Gill as architects.
facts.quote: Pearl River Tower (珠江城大厦) is a 71-story, 309.6 m (1,016 ft), clean technology neofuturistic skyscraper at the junction of Jinsui Road/Zhujiang Avenue West, Tianhe, Guangzhou, China. The tower's architecture and engineering were performed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill with Adrian D. Smith and Gordon Gill (now at their own firm, AS+GG) as architects.

facts.fact: Ground broke on 8 September 2006 and construction was completed in March 2011.
facts.quote: Ground broke on the tower on 8 September 2006 and construction was completed in March 2011.

facts.fact: The design follows four steps toward zero energy: reduction, absorption, reclamation and generation.
facts.quote: There were four steps in the approach to the Pearl River Tower's high-performance design: reduction, absorption, reclamation, and generation. These steps were put in place to achieve the goal of being a zero-energy building.

facts.fact: The tower's shape funnels wind through four large turbines, generating up to 15 times more energy than freestanding turbines.
facts.quote: The Pearl River Tower's design enables it to funnel wind through four large wind turbines to generate up to 15 times more energy than regular freestanding turbines.

facts.fact: Its broadest face is set perpendicular to Guangzhou's prevailing southerly wind.
facts.quote: To make the most of the prevailing wind direction, it was essential to place the building's broadest face at a perpendicular angle to the prevailing wind.

facts.fact: A double-skin façade lets solar heat through its outer skin while the inner skin prevents solar gain.
facts.quote: There is a double-skin façade in place, meaning the walls have two layers: the outer skin has a high permeability for solar heat to allow it in, while the inner skin prevents solar gain. This is referred to as a double curtain wall.

facts.fact: It is the largest radiant-cooled office building in the world.
facts.quote: The largest radiant-cooled office building in the world

facts.fact: Fire codes and regulations forced changes to the original design; the finished 212,165 m² building uses about 40% of the energy a typical building of its size would.
facts.quote: Complications with fire codes and regulations resulted in the original design being amended. In its final state, the 212,165 m2 building uses around 40% of the energy that a building of its size would typically use.

facts.fact: An art museum within the Moorilla winery on the Berriedale peninsula in Hobart, the largest privately funded museum in the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: The Museum of Old and New Art (MONA) is an art museum located within the Moorilla winery on the Berriedale peninsula in Hobart, Tasmania, Australia. It is the largest privately funded museum in the Southern Hemisphere.

facts.fact: MONA officially opened on 21 January 2011.
facts.quote: MONA was officially opened on 21 January 2011.

facts.fact: The single-storey building looks modest at street level, but a spiral staircase leads down to three larger levels of display spaces built into the cliffs.
facts.quote: The single-storey MONA building appears at street level to be dominated by its surroundings, but its interior possesses a spiral staircase that leads down to three larger levels of labyrinthine display spaces built into the side of the cliffs around Berriedale peninsula.

facts.fact: It was built mostly underground to preserve the setting of two Roy Grounds houses on the property.
facts.quote: The decision to build it largely underground was taken, according to Walsh, to preserve the heritage setting of the two Roy Grounds houses on the property.

facts.fact: There are no windows, and the atmosphere is intentionally ominous.
facts.quote: There are no windows and the atmosphere is intentionally ominous.

facts.fact: Visitors descend first and then work their way back up to the surface, the reverse of the Guggenheim's spiral.
facts.quote: To see the art, the visitor must work back upwards towards the surface, a trajectory that has been contrasted with the descending spiral that many visitors follow in New York's Guggenheim Museum.

facts.fact: Most visitors arrive by ferry up the River Derwent.
facts.quote: Most visitors approach by ferry up the River Derwent.

facts.fact: Fender Katsalidis won the 2012 Sir Zelman Cowen Award for Public Architecture for MONA.
facts.quote: 2012 Sir Zelman Cowen Award for Public Architecture — Museum of Old and New Art (MONA)

facts.fact: A 420.5 m, 88-storey skyscraper in Lujiazui, Pudong, holding a shopping mall, offices and the Grand Hyatt Shanghai hotel.
facts.quote: The Jin Mao Tower (simplified Chinese: 金茂大厦; traditional Chinese: 金茂大廈; pinyin: Jīnmào Dàshà; Shanghainese: Cinmeu Dagho; lit. 'Golden Prosperity Building'), also known as the Jinmao Building or Jinmao Tower, is a 420.5-meter-tall (1,380 ft), 88-story (93 if counting the floors in the spire) landmark skyscraper in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai, China. It contains a shopping mall, offices and the Grand Hyatt Shanghai hotel which starts from the 53rd floor; at the time of completion it was the highest hotel in the world.

facts.fact: Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, its postmodern form draws on the tiered pagoda, stepping back in a rhythmic pattern as it rises.
facts.quote: It was designed by the Chicago firm of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM). Its postmodern form, whose complexity rises as it ascends, draws on traditional Chinese architecture such as the tiered pagoda, gently stepping back to create a rhythmic pattern as it rises.

facts.fact: Its proportions revolve around the number 8, linked with prosperity in Chinese culture; the floors form 16 segments, each 1/8 shorter than the base.
facts.quote: Like the Petronas Towers in Malaysia, the building's proportions revolve around the number 8, associated with prosperity in Chinese culture. The 88 floors (93 if the spire floors are counted) are divided into 16 segments, each of which is 1/8 shorter than the 16-story base.

facts.fact: An octagonal concrete core is ringed by 8 composite supercolumns and 8 steel columns, tied together by outrigger trusses.
facts.quote: The tower is built around an octagon-shaped concrete shear wall core surrounded by 8 exterior composite supercolumns and 8 exterior steel columns. Three sets of 8 two-story high outrigger trusses connect the columns to the core at six of the floors to provide additional support.

facts.fact: Its foundations rest on 1,062 steel piles driven 83.5 m deep, the longest then used for a building on land.
facts.quote: The foundations rest on 1,062 high-capacity steel piles driven 83.5 m (274 ft) deep in the ground to compensate for poor upper-strata soil conditions. At the time of construction, these were the longest steel piles ever used for a land-based building.

facts.fact: The curtain wall of glass, stainless steel, aluminium and granite is criss-crossed by aluminium-pipe latticework.
facts.quote: The exterior curtain wall is made of glass, stainless steel, aluminum, and granite and is criss-crossed by complex latticework cladding made of aluminum alloy pipes.

facts.fact: The hotel's barrel-vaulted atrium rises from the 56th to the 87th floor, lined with spiralling corridors, about 115 m high.
facts.quote: The Hyatt's famous barrel-vaulted atrium starts at the 56th floor and extends upwards to the 87th. Lined with 28 annular corridors and staircases arrayed in a spiral, it is 27 m (89 ft) in diameter with a clear height of approximately 115 m (377 ft).

facts.fact: It was dedicated on 28 August 1998, a date chosen with the number 8 in mind.
facts.quote: Official dedication was August 28, 1998, a date also chosen with the number 8 in mind.

facts.fact: A memorial in Nagasaki, next to the Atomic Bomb Museum, built to remember and pray for those who died in the 1945 atomic bombing.
facts.quote: Like its counterpart in Hiroshima, the hall was constructed as a place to remember and pray for those who died in the 1945 atomic bombing, with photos, memoirs and personal accounts of the event.

facts.fact: Akira Kuryu designed it; it was built between November 2000 and December 2002.
facts.quote: Designed by architect Akira Kuryu, the memorial was constructed between November 2000 and December 2002.

facts.fact: Its rooms are underground, including a remembrance hall where 12 pillars of light stand for hope for peace.
facts.quote: The subterranean interior of the building contains a reference area, a large conference room, an anteroom with a bank of monitors showing photographs of the victims, and a stylized remembrance hall in which 12 pillars of light symbolize hope for peace.

facts.fact: From outside, the top is mostly a tree-lined basin of water through which the 12 light pillars rise.
facts.quote: As viewed from the outside, the top of the memorial consists mainly of a tree-lined basin of water through which the 12 pillars of light continue to rise from below.

facts.fact: At night 70,000 fibre-optic lights glow across the water, symbolising the victims.
facts.quote: At night, 70,000 fiber optic lights are illuminated across the surface of the water, symbolizing the victims.

facts.fact: An upper level lets visitors look down into the Remembrance Hall.
facts.quote: An upper level serves as an abbreviated tour, with diary excerpts and a viewing station allowing visitors to view the Remembrance Hall from above.

facts.fact: A museum in memory of those killed in the Nanjing Massacre after the city fell to the Japanese army on 13 December 1937.
facts.quote: The Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders is a museum to memorialize those that were killed in the Nanjing Massacre by the Imperial Japanese Army in and around the then-capital of China, Nanjing, after it fell on 13 December 1937.

facts.fact: It stands at Jiangdongmen, near a mass burial site called the 'pit of ten thousand people'.
facts.quote: It is located in the southwestern corner of  downtown Nanjing known as Jiangdongmen (江东门), near a site where thousands of bodies were buried, called the "pit of ten thousand people" (simplified Chinese: 万人坑; traditional Chinese: 萬人坑; pinyin: wàn rén kēng).

facts.fact: It was built in 1985 by the Nanjing government and enlarged and renovated in 1995.
facts.quote: The Nanjing Memorial Hall was built in 1985 by the Nanjing Municipal Government in memory of the three hundred thousand victims of the massacre. In 1995, it was enlarged and renovated.

facts.fact: Qi Kang designed the memorial hall, in phases in 1983–1985 and 1995.
facts.quote: Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall, 1983–1985 (Phase 1), 1995 (Phase 2)

facts.fact: It uses architecture, sculpture and video alongside historical records to show what happened.
facts.quote: The memorial exhibits historical records and objects, and uses architecture, sculptures, and videos to illustrate what happened during the Nanjing Massacre.

facts.fact: It has three parts: outdoor exhibits, sheltered skeletal remains of victims, and an exhibition hall of documents.
facts.quote: The memorial consists of three major parts: outdoor exhibits, sheltered skeletal remains of victims, and an exhibition hall of historical documents.

facts.fact: The exhibition hall is tomb-like and half underground.
facts.quote: The tomb-like exhibition hall, half underground, contains more than 1000 items related to the massacre, including an immense collection of pictures, objects, charts, and photographs.

facts.fact: The site covers about 28,000 m², with about 3,000 m² of building floor space.
facts.quote: It occupies a total area of approximately twenty-eight thousand square meters, including about three thousand square meters of building floor space.

facts.fact: An elevated linear park in Seoul built on a former highway overpass, about 1 km long and lined with 24,000 plants.
facts.quote: Seoullo 7017 (Korean: 서울로 7017), also known as the Seoul Skygarden or Skypark, is an elevated linear park in Seoul, built atop a former highway overpass (Seoul Station Overpass, Korean: 서울역고가도로). The path, which is about 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) in length and lined with 24,000 plants, is similar to New York City's High Line.

facts.fact: It was designed by the Dutch firm MVRDV and opened in May 2017.
facts.quote: Skygarden was designed by MVRDV, a Dutch firm, and opened in May 2017.

facts.fact: The disused overpass closed in 2015 and crosses Seoul Station diagonally, 17 m above the street.
facts.quote: The disused overpass closed in 2015 and cuts diagonally across Seoul Station at 17 metres (56 ft) above street level.

facts.fact: '70' refers to 1970, when the flyover was dedicated; '17' to its 17 connecting walkways and its 2017 opening.
facts.quote: The "70" in the name comes from 1970, the year the flyover was dedicated, while the "17" is  a reference to both the number of walkways connected to it and its opening in 2017.

facts.fact: The park includes gardens, terraces and exhibitions, with over 24,000 plants of 228 species of trees, shrubs and flowers.
facts.quote: The park includes gardens, terraces, and exhibitions, and was promised to "feature over 24,085 plants representing 228 species of trees, shrubs and flowers found in and outside Korea."

facts.fact: Mayor Park Won-soon pushed for the US$52 million skypark as a complement to the Cheonggyecheon Stream restoration.
facts.quote: Seoul mayor Park Won-soon pushed for the US$52 million skypark to be completed as a complement to Seoul's Cheonggyecheon Stream restoration project, organized under previous mayor Lee Myung-bak.

facts.fact: Rogier van der Heide designed a deep blue night lighting scheme for it.
facts.quote: Rogier van der Heide designed a deep blue lighting scheme that offers visitors a scenic experience at night.

facts.fact: It is Taiwan's largest cultural facility and the world's largest performing arts venue under one roof.
facts.quote: It is the largest cultural facility in Taiwan, the world's largest performing art theater under one roof, and the first national-level performing arts venue in southern Taiwan.

facts.fact: Dutch architect Francine Houben designed the main building, with four halls: an opera house, concert hall, playhouse and recital hall.
facts.quote: The main building was designed by Dutch architect Francine Houben and includes four indoor performance halls, which are as follows: an Opera House with 2,236 seats, a Concert Hall with 1,981 seats, a Playhouse with 1,209 seats, and a Recital Hall with 434 seats.

facts.fact: The design firm Mecanoo won the design and construction rights in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, the design firm Mecanoo Architecten won the design and construction rights.

facts.fact: Houben drew on Weiwuying's banyan tree grove, letting the public enter from all directions.
facts.quote: Architect Francine Houben incorporated the design of the Weiwuying banyan tree grove, allowing the public to enter the venue from all directions.

facts.fact: The 35,000 m² curved roof is made of 4,500 aluminium alloy panels.
facts.quote: The roof features a 35,000 square meter curved surface roof, constructed with 4,500 aluminum alloy panels, making it the world's largest comprehensive performance venue under a single roof.

facts.fact: The curved steel-skinned interior walls were built with Kaohsiung's shipbuilding techniques, recalling its harbour.
facts.quote: The curved shapes are built using shipbuilding techniques, reflecting the maritime imagery of Kaohsiung Harbor and the historical shipbuilding industry.

facts.fact: The four halls and an outdoor theatre are linked by Banyan Plaza.
facts.quote: Inside the venue building, four performance halls and an outdoor theater are interconnected by Banyan Plaza.

facts.fact: The site was once a military training base, evacuated in 1979.
facts.quote: However, the Military Council of Nationalist Kuomintang (KMT) determined that the camp was no longer suitable for military purposes in 1979, which led to the evacuation of the camp.

facts.fact: A skyscraper in Johannesburg's central business district, also known as the Hanging Building.
facts.quote: The Standard Bank Centre (also known as the Hanging Building or the 78 Fox Street) is a skyscraper in Johannesburg, South Africa.

facts.fact: A 139 m skyscraper in Johannesburg, built from 1966 to 1968.
facts.quote: Construction of the building started in 1966 and was completed in 1968. It is 139 m (456 ft) tall.

facts.fact: It was built from the top down: after the central core went up, the floors were hung from cantilevered arms, the top floors first.
facts.quote: The building was built from the top-down, meaning that after the central core was built, the floors were suspended from cantilevered arms with the top floors added first, followed by each lower floor.

facts.fact: To use as little ground as possible, the designers adopted the 'hanging' design.
facts.quote: To keep space used to a minimum, they adopted the "hanging" design.

facts.fact: Helmut Hentrich and Hubert Petschnigg designed it with the engineer Ove Arup.
facts.quote: The challenge for the designers - the German architect Helmut Hentrich (1905–2001) and the Austrian architect Hubert Petschnigg (1913–1997), who planned the skyscraper in collaboration with the British-Danish-Norwegian engineer Ove Arup (1895–1988) - was to find a spacious square in the crowded Johannesburg CBD to anchor an office building.

facts.fact: Apart from its concrete core, it is built of precast reinforced concrete slabs, glass and steel.
facts.quote: Apart from the concrete core tower, the Standard Bank Centre was built by Concor of precast reinforced concrete slabs, glass, and steel.

facts.fact: A special slewing crane lifted and fixed a quarter of each floor at a time.
facts.quote: A special slewing crane was designed for the project to lift and mount a quarter of each floor level.

facts.fact: The hanging design means the offices need no pillars.
facts.quote: The office is 9.7 m wide. The hanging design eliminates the need for pillars.

facts.fact: Tinted, laminated double glazing protects against the sun, and 60 cm balustrades make cleaning the outer pane easy.
facts.quote: The windows use tinted glass with laminated double glazing for sunlight protection. No special arrangements need to be made for window cleaning, since the 60-cm balustrades make cleaning the outer pane easy.

facts.fact: Three thin towers on a promontory into the Persian Gulf in Kuwait City, the last group in the Kuwait Water Towers system.
facts.quote: The Kuwait Towers are a group of three  thin towers in Kuwait City, standing on a promontory into the Persian Gulf. They were the sixth, and last, group in the larger Kuwait Water Towers system of 34 towers (33 store water; one stores equipment), and were built in a style considerably different from the other five groups.

facts.fact: Malene Bjørn designed them for a water distribution project run by the Swedish firm VBB.
facts.quote: The Kuwait Towers were designed by Danish architect Malene Bjørn as part of a water distribution project run by the Swedish engineering company VBB (renamed Sweco in 1997).

facts.fact: Three of ten designs were presented to the Emir, who chose the one that was built.
facts.quote: Out of ten different designs, three were presented to the Amir, who chose the design built.

facts.fact: The main tower is 187 m high and carries two spheres.
facts.quote: The main tower is 187 metres (614 ft) high and carries two spheres.

facts.fact: The towers are built of reinforced and prestressed concrete; work ran from 1971 to 1976, and the main tower opened on 1 March 1979.
facts.quote: The towers were built of reinforced concrete and prestressed concrete. Building took place from 1971 to 1976 and the main tower was opened to the public on 1 March 1979.

facts.fact: About 41,000 enamelled steel discs in eight shades of blue, green and grey cover the spheres, recalling the tiled domes of historic mosques.
facts.quote: Approximately 41,000 enameled steel discs cover the three spheres in eight shades of blue, green and gray, recalling the tiled domes of historic mosques.

facts.fact: The architect said the group stands for humanity and technology, symbolised by the globe and the rocket.
facts.quote: According to the architect, the Kuwait Tower group refers to ideals of humanity and technology, symbolised by the globe and the rocket.

facts.fact: In 1980 the Kuwait Water Towers, including these towers, won one of the first Aga Khan Awards for Architecture.
facts.quote: In 1980, the Kuwait Water Towers system, including the Kuwait Towers, was an inaugural recipient of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture.

facts.fact: The museum holds over 66,000 works from 30 centuries of art, from pre-Hispanic sculpture to European old masters and Rodin.
facts.quote: It has over 66,000 works from 30 centuries of art including sculptures from Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica, 19th- and 20th-century Mexican art and an extensive repertoire of works by European old masters and masters of modern western art such as Auguste Rodin, Salvador Dalí, Bartolomé Esteban Murillo and Tintoretto.

facts.fact: The new building in Plaza Carso, Nuevo Polanco, was designed by Mexican architect Fernando Romero and opened in 2011.
facts.quote: The new building in Plaza Carso in the Nuevo Polanco district was designed by the Mexican architect Fernando Romero, son-in-law of Lebanese-Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim Helu, and opened in 2011.

facts.fact: The 46 m, six-storey building is covered in 16,000 hexagonal aluminium tiles.
facts.quote: The building is a 46-metre-high (151 ft) six-story building covered by 16,000 hexagonal aluminum tiles.

facts.fact: It was engineered with Ove Arup and Frank Gehry and cost $70 million.
facts.quote: The new building was designed by the Mexican architect Fernando Romero, who is married to a daughter of Carlos Slim, engineered with Ove Arup and Frank Gehry, and cost $70 million to build.

facts.fact: Its weight is carried by an exoskeleton of 28 curved vertical steel columns and seven encircling beams.
facts.quote: The weight of the building is held by an exoskeleton of 28 vertical curved steel columns and seven beams encircling the structure built by a Slim-owned company that manufactures offshore oil rigs.

facts.fact: A narrow entrance opens into a large white gallery, and the top floor is open to daylight.
facts.quote: The museum has a narrow entrance that opens into a large white gallery. The top floor of the building is opened so that it is illuminated by sunlight during the daytime.

facts.fact: Each of the museum's six floors has a distinct shape.
facts.quote: Each of the six floors of the museum is distinctly shaped.

facts.fact: It holds the largest collection of Rodin casts outside France.
facts.quote: The museum holds the largest collection of casts of sculptures by Auguste Rodin outside France, and the world's largest private collection of his art.
